translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong ordered that he be buried near Dingling and granted his son Huang a fief of one hundred fifty taxable households.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, given the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, he was given the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 元忠始名真宰，以諸生見高宗，高宗慰遣，不知謝即出，儀舉自安，帝目送謂薛元超曰：「是子未習朝廷儀，然名不虛謂，真宰相也。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was originally named Zhenzai. As a student he was received by Emperor Gaozong; the Emperor consoled and dismissed him, and not knowing to bow thanks he went out—his demeanor composed and at ease. The Emperor watched him go and said to Xue Yuanchao: "This youth has not learned court etiquette, yet his name is no empty claim—truly a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was originally named Zhenzai. As a student he was received by Emperor Gaozong; the Emperor consoled and dismissed him, and not knowing to bow in thanks he simply walked out, composed and at ease. The Emperor watched him go and said to Xue Yuanchao: "This youth has not learned court etiquette, yet his name is no empty boast—he is truly a chief minister in the making.

sentences.zh: 避武後母諱，改今名。

translations.literal: To avoid the taboo on Empress Wu's mother's name, he changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the taboo on Empress Wu's mother's name, he changed to his present name.

sentences.zh: 韋安石，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi — Anshi was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖孝寬，為周大司空、鄖國公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaokuan served as Grand Minister of Works of Zhou and Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiaokuan served as Grand Minister of Works under Zhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 祖津，隋大業末為民部侍郎，與元文都等留守洛，拒李密，戰上東門，為密禽。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jin, at the end of the Sui Daye reign, was Vice Minister of Revenue; with Yuan Wendu and others he held Luoyang, resisted Li Mi, fought at the Upper East Gate, and was captured by Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jin, at the end of the Sui Daye era, was Vice Minister of Revenue; with Yuan Wendu and others he held Luoyang, resisted Li Mi, fought at the Upper East Gate, and was captured by Mi.

sentences.zh: 後王世充殺文都而津獨免，密敗，復歸洛。

translations.literal: Later Wang Shichong killed Wendu but Jin alone escaped; when Mi was defeated, he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Shichong killed Wendu but Jin alone was spared; when Mi was defeated, he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 世充平，高祖素與津善，授諫議大夫，檢校黃門侍郎，陵州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, the Founding Emperor, who had long been on good terms with Jin, appointed him Remonstrating Grand Master, Acting Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prefect of Lingzhou—he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong was pacified, the Founding Emperor, who had long been on good terms with Jin, appointed him Remonstrating Grand Master, Acting Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prefect of Lingzhou, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 父琬，仕為成州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wan served as Prefect of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan served as Prefect of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 安石舉明經，調乾封尉，雍州長史蘇良嗣器之。

translations.literal: Anshi passed the Mingjing examination, was assigned as marshal of Qianfeng, and Su Liangsi, Chief Administrator of Yongzhou, recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi passed the Mingjing examination and was assigned as marshal of Qianfeng; Su Liangsi, Chief Administrator of Yongzhou, recognized his talent.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，遷雍州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, he was transferred to Army Staff Officer of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang, he was transferred to Army Staff Officer of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 良嗣當國，謂安石曰：「大才當大用，徒勞州縣可乎？」

translations.literal: When Liangsi held power, he said to Anshi: "Great talent deserves great use—is it fitting to waste yourself in counties and prefectures?
translations.idiomatic: When Liangsi held power, he said to Anshi: "Great talent deserves great use—is it fitting to waste yourself in county and prefectural posts?

sentences.zh: 薦於武後，擢膳部員外郎，遷并州司馬，有善政，後手制勞問，陟拜德、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: He recommended him to Empress Wu; Anshi was promoted to Surplus Director in the Ministry of Rites, transferred to Deputy Prefect of Bingzhou, administered well; the Empress sent a personal edict of commendation and promoted him to Prefect of De and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended him to Empress Wu; Anshi was promoted to Surplus Director in the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to Deputy Prefect of Bingzhou, where he governed well. The Empress sent a personal edict of commendation and promoted him to Prefect of De and Zheng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安石性方重，不茍言笑，其政尚清嚴，吏民尊畏。

translations.literal: Anshi's nature was upright and solemn; he was sparing of words and laughter. His governance prized clarity and severity; officials and commoners revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was upright and solemn by nature, sparing of words and laughter. His governance prized clarity and severity, and officials and commoners alike revered and feared him.

sentences.zh: 久視中，遷文昌右丞，以鸞臺侍郎同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，兼太子左庶子，仍侍讀，尋知納言事。

translations.literal: During the Jiushi reign, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat of the Brilliant Hall; made Co-Grand Chancellor with the title Palace Secretary, concurrently Left Sub-governor of the Crown Prince, still serving as Reader; soon he also handled the affairs of the Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiushi reign, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat of the Brilliant Hall and made Co-Grand Chancellor with the title Palace Secretary, concurrently Left Sub-governor of the Crown Prince and still serving as Reader; soon he also handled the affairs of the Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時二張及武三思寵橫，安石數折辱之。

translations.literal: At that time the Two Zhangs and Wu Sansi enjoyed extravagant favor; Anshi repeatedly shamed and humiliated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Two Zhangs and Wu Sansi enjoyed extravagant favor; Anshi repeatedly shamed and humiliated them.

sentences.zh: 會侍宴殿中，易之引蜀商宋霸子等博塞後前，安石跪奏「商等賤類，不當戲殿上。」

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet in the hall, Yizhi brought in Sichuan merchants Song Bazi and others to gamble before and behind; Anshi kneeled and memorialized: "Merchants and such low people should not play in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending a banquet in the palace hall, Zhang Yizhi brought in Sichuan merchants Song Bazi and others to gamble about the room; Anshi kneeled and memorialized: "Merchants and such lowborn people should not be playing in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 顧左右引出，坐皆失色，後以安石辭正，改容慰勉。

translations.literal: He looked to attendants and had them led out; all present turned pale; the Empress, finding Anshi's words correct, changed her expression and comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: He looked to the attendants and had them led out; all present turned pale. The Empress, finding Anshi's words correct, changed her expression and comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎陸元方自以為不及，退告人曰：「韋公真宰相。」

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Lu Yuanfang considered himself inferior; leaving, he told others: "Lord Wei is a true chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Lu Yuanfang considered himself inferior to Anshi; leaving the hall, he told others: "Lord Wei is a true chief minister.

sentences.zh: 後嘗幸興泰宮，議趨疾道，安石曰：「此道板築所成，非自然之固。

translations.literal: Later while visiting Xingtai Palace, when a shortcut path was proposed, Anshi said: "This path is built of planks and earthworks—not a natural solid ground.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while visiting Xingtai Palace, when a shortcut path was proposed, Anshi said: "This path is built of planks and earthworks—it is not naturally solid ground.

sentences.zh: 千金子且誡垂堂，況萬乘可輕乘危哉？」

translations.literal: Even a man worth a thousand gold cautions against sitting beneath a cornice—how much more should the ruler of ten thousand chariots lightly venture into peril?"
translations.idiomatic: Even a man worth a thousand gold cautions against sitting beneath a cornice—how much less should the ruler of ten thousand chariots lightly venture into peril?"

sentences.zh: 後為回輦。

translations.literal: The Empress turned her carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress turned her carriage back.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，同鳳閣鸞臺三品，俄又知納言，檢校揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, made Third Rank under the Phoenix Pavilion and Palace Secretariat; soon again handled the Palace Secretary, Acting Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chang'an, he was made Third Rank under the Phoenix Pavilion and Palace Secretariat; soon he again handled the Palace Secretary and served as Acting Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，罷政事，俄復同三品，遷中書令，兼相王府長史，封鄖國公，賜封三百戶，加特進，為侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, removed from government; soon restored to Third Rank, transferred to Chief Minister of the Central Secretariat, concurrently Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, granted three hundred fief households, given Special Advancement, made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, he was removed from government; soon restored to Third Rank, transferred to Chief Minister of the Central Secretariat, concurrently Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, enfeoffed as Duke of Yun with three hundred fief households, given Special Advancement, and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 中宗與韋後以正月望夜幸其第，賚賜不貲。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong and Empress Wei on the fifteenth night of the first month visited his residence; gifts and rewards were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited his residence on the fifteenth night of the first month; the gifts and rewards were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸安樂公主池，主請禦船，安石曰：「禦輕舟，乘不測，非帝王事。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once visited Princess Anle's pond; the Princess asked him to board a boat. Anshi said: "Boarding a light skiff, venturing into the uncertain—this is not the affair of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once visited Princess Anle's pond; the Princess asked him to board a boat. Anshi said: "Boarding a light skiff and venturing into the uncertain—this is not fitting for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，授太子少保，改封郇國，復為侍中、中書令，進開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended, Anshi was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, enfeoffed as Duke of Xun, again made Palace Attendant and Chief Minister, advanced to Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Anshi was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, enfeoffed as Duke of Xun, again made Palace Attendant and Chief Minister, and advanced to Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太平公主有異謀，欲引安石，數因其婿唐晙邀之，拒不往。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping had a secret plot and wished to win Anshi; repeatedly through her son-in-law Tang Jun she invited him—he refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping had a secret plot and wished to win Anshi over; repeatedly through her son-in-law Tang Jun she invited him, but he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 帝一日召安石曰：「朝廷傾心東宮，卿胡不察？」

translations.literal: One day the Emperor summoned Anshi and said: "The court is devoted to the Eastern Palace—why have you not noticed?
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor summoned Anshi and said: "The court is devoted to the Eastern Palace—why have you not noticed?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太子仁孝，天下所稱，且有大功。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial, praised throughout the realm, and has rendered great service.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial, praised throughout the realm, and has rendered great service.

sentences.zh: 陛下今安得亡國語？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty now utter words that foretell a state's ruin?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty now utter words that foretell a state's ruin?

sentences.zh: 此必太平公主計也。」

translations.literal: This must be Princess Taiping's scheme."
translations.idiomatic: This must be Princess Taiping's scheme."

sentences.zh: 帝矍然曰：「卿勿言，朕知之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor started and said: "Say no more—I understand."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor started and said: "Say no more—I understand."

sentences.zh: 主竊聞，乃構飛變，欲訊之，賴郭元振保護，免。

translations.literal: The Princess secretly heard, then fabricated false charges and sought to interrogate him; thanks to Guo Yuanzhen's protection, he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess secretly overheard and then fabricated false charges, seeking to interrogate him; thanks to Guo Yuanzhen's protection, he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射兼太子賓客、同三品，俄罷政事，留守東都。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince, Third Rank; soon removed from government, left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince and Third Rank; soon removed from government and left to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會妻薛怨婿婢，笞殺之，為御史中丞楊茂謙所劾，下遷蒲州刺史，徙青州。

translations.literal: It happened that his wife Lady Xue, resentful of her son-in-law's maid, whipped her to death; impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yang Maoqian, he was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that his wife Lady Xue, resentful of her son-in-law's maid, whipped her to death; impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yang Maoqian, he was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou and then transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 安石在蒲，太常卿姜皎有所請，拒之。

translations.literal: While Anshi was at Pu, Grand Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Jiao made a request; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: While Anshi was at Pu, Grand Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Jiao made a request of him; Anshi refused.

sentences.zh: 皎弟晦為中丞，以安石昔相中宗，受遺制，而宗楚客、韋溫擅削相王輔政語，安石無所建正，諷侍御史洪子輿劾舉，子輿以更赦不從。

translations.literal: Jiao's brother Hui was Censor-in-Chief; because Anshi had once served as Zhongzong's chief minister and received the final edict, yet Zong Chuke and Wei Wen arbitrarily excised the language on the Prince of Xiang assisting in government and Anshi made no correction—Hui prompted Attending Censor Hong Ziyu to impeach him; Ziyu withheld because of a recent amnesty, but Hui would not accept that.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's brother Hui was Censor-in-Chief; because Anshi had once served as Zhongzong's chief minister and received the final edict, yet Zong Chuke and Wei Wen had arbitrarily excised the language on the Prince of Xiang assisting in government and Anshi had made no correction—Hui prompted Attending Censor Hong Ziyu to impeach him. Ziyu withheld because of a recent amnesty, but Hui would not accept that.

sentences.zh: 監察御史郭震奏之，有詔與韋嗣立、趙彥昭等皆貶，安石為沔州別駕。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Guo Zhen memorialized; an edict demoted Wei Silie, Zhao Yanzhao, and others together; Anshi was made Vice Prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Guo Zhen memorialized the matter; an edict demoted Wei Silie, Zhao Yanzhao, and others together, and Anshi was made Vice Prefect of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 皎又奏安石護作定陵，有所盜沒，詔籍其贓。

translations.literal: Jiao again memorialized that Anshi, overseeing construction of Dingling, had embezzled; an edict ordered confiscation of the ill-gotten gains.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao again memorialized that Anshi, while overseeing construction of Dingling, had embezzled funds; an edict ordered confiscation of the ill-gotten gains.

sentences.zh: 安石嘆曰：「只須我死乃已。」

translations.literal: Anshi sighed: "Only my death will end this.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi sighed: "Only my death will end this.

sentences.zh: 發憤卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in indignant vexation, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in indignant vexation, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，贈蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, posthumously granted Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, he was posthumously granted the title Prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，加贈左僕射、郇國公，謚文貞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, further posthumously granted Left Vice Director and Duke of Xun; posthumous title Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, he was further posthumously granted Left Vice Director and Duke of Xun, with the posthumous title Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 二子：陟，、斌。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhi and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhi and Bin.

sentences.zh: 子 陟陟字殷卿，與弟斌俱秀敏異常童。

translations.literal: Son Zhi — Zhi, courtesy name Yinqing, with his younger brother Bin were both remarkably brilliant as children.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi — Zhi, courtesy name Yinqing — and his younger brother Bin were both remarkably brilliant as children.

sentences.zh: 安石晚有子，愛之。

translations.literal: Anshi had sons late in life and doted on them.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had sons late in life and doted on them.

sentences.zh: 神龍一年，安石為中書令，陟甫十歲，授溫王府東閣祭酒、朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, when Anshi was Chief Minister, Zhi was just ten years old and was granted Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Wen's household and Grand Master for Dispersal of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, when Anshi was Chief Minister, Zhi was just ten years old and was granted the posts of Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Wen's household and Grand Master for Dispersal of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 風格方整，善文辭，書有楷法，一時知名士皆與遊。

translations.literal: His bearing was square and proper, skilled in literary composition, his calligraphy had standard rules — all the renowned scholars of the age associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with upright, orderly bearing, excelled at literary composition, and wrote calligraphy in proper standard script. All the celebrated men of letters of the day sought his company.

sentences.zh: 開元中居喪，以父不得誌歿，乃與斌杜門不出八年。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, while in mourning, because his father had died without fulfilling his ambitions, he and Bin shut their doors and did not go out for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, while observing mourning, he learned that his father had died without ever realizing his ambitions. He and Bin thereupon shut their doors and remained in seclusion for eight years.

sentences.zh: 親友更往敦曉，乃強調為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Friends and relatives repeatedly came to urge and enlighten him, until he was forcibly transferred to be Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Friends and relatives came again and again to counsel him, until at last he was pressed into service and appointed Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 宋璟見陟嘆曰：「盛德遺範，盡在是矣。」

translations.literal: When Song Jing saw Zhi he sighed and said: "The lofty virtue and enduring example — all of it is embodied in this man.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing saw Zhi, he sighed and said, "The full measure of lofty virtue and enduring example is embodied in this man.

sentences.zh: 累除吏部郎中，中書令張九齡引為舍人，與孫逖、梁涉並司書命，時號得才。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel; Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling recruited him as Attendant Drafting Scribe; together with Sun Ti and Liang She he jointly managed the drafting of edicts — at the time they were acclaimed as having obtained talent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Director in the Ministry of Personnel. Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling brought him in as Attendant Drafting Scribe, and together with Sun Ti and Liang She he shared responsibility for drafting imperial edicts. At the time they were praised as men who had truly found talent.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 陟於鑒裁尤長。

translations.literal: Zhi was especially accomplished at discernment and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was especially skilled at discernment and evaluation.

sentences.zh: 故事，取人以一日試為高下。

translations.literal: By precedent, candidates were assessed for rank and station on the basis of one day's examination.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, candidates were ranked high or low according to a single day's examination.

sentences.zh: 陟許自通所工，先就其能試之，已乃程考，由是無遺材。

translations.literal: Zhi allowed people to declare what they excelled at, first tested them on their abilities, and only then conducted standardized examinations — hence no talented person was overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi allowed candidates to declare their own strengths, tested them first in those areas, and only then applied the standard examination. In this way no capable person was overlooked.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，選人多偽集，與正調相冒，陟有風采，擿辨無不伏者，黜正數百員，銓綜號為公平。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel — many candidates had falsified credentials and usurped regular appointment quotas; Zhi had commanding presence, and in exposing and distinguishing cases none failed to submit; he dismissed several hundred from regular appointment rolls, and his evaluation and selection was acclaimed as fair.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, many candidates had falsified their records and encroached on regular appointment quotas. Zhi had a commanding presence, and in exposing fraud none failed to submit. He struck several hundred from the regular rolls, and his selection process was acclaimed as fair.

sentences.zh: 然任威嚴，或至詈詰，議者訾其峻。

translations.literal: Yet he relied on stern authority, sometimes going so far as to revile and interrogate — critics faulted him for severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relied on stern authority and sometimes went so far as to revile and cross-examine candidates. Critics faulted him for excessive severity.

sentences.zh: 又自以門品可坐階三公，居常簡貴，視僚黨涘然；

translations.literal: Moreover, considering his family status sufficient to reach the ranks of the Three Dukes, in daily conduct he was aloof and lofty, looking upon colleagues with cold detachment;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, believing his family standing entitled him to rise to the rank of one of the Three Dukes, he was habitually aloof and lofty in manner, and looked upon his colleagues with cold indifference;

sentences.zh: 其以道誼合，雖後進布衣與均禮。

translations.literal: yet for those aligned with him in principle and friendship, even juniors in plain cloth received equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: yet toward those united with him in principle and friendship, he showed equal courtesy even to young men in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 李林甫惡其名高，恐逼己，出為襄陽太守，徙河南采訪使，以判官員錫善訊覆，支使韋元甫工書奏，時號「員推韋狀」，陟皆倚任之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu resented his high renown, fearing he might supplant himself, and sent him out as Administrator of Xiangyang, then transferred him to be Inspector of Henan; his aide Yuan Xi excelled at interrogation and review, his dispatch officer Wei Yuanfu was skilled at memorial drafts — at the time they were called "Yuan handles the interrogations, Wei the drafts," and Zhi relied on both.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu resented Zhi's high reputation and feared he might be displaced by him, so he sent Zhi out as Administrator of Xiangyang and then transferred him to Inspector of Henan. His aide Yuan Xi excelled at interrogation and review, and his dispatch officer Wei Yuanfu was skilled at drafting memorials. At the time people called them "Yuan for interrogations, Wei for drafts," and Zhi relied on both men.

sentences.zh: 俄襲郇國公，坐事貶守鐘離、義陽，後為河東太守。

translations.literal: Soon he inherited the title of Duke of Xun, but was demoted on account of an offense to Administrator of Zhongli and Yiyang, and later became Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inherited the title of Duke of Xun, but was demoted on account of an offense to serve as Administrator of Zhongli and Yiyang. He later became Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 以失職，內怏怏，乃毀廉隅，頗餉謝權幸欲自結。

translations.literal: Distressed at losing office, inwardly resentful, he compromised his integrity and frequently sent gifts to powerful favorites seeking to attach himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed at losing office and brooding inwardly, he compromised his integrity and frequently sent gifts to powerful favorites in hopes of winning their favor.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，入考華清宮，楊國忠忌其才，謂拾遺吳豸之曰：「子能發陟罪乎？

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, when he came for examination at Huaqing Palace, Yang Guozhong resented his talent and said to Remonstrance Officer Wu Zhizhi: "Can you expose Zhi's crimes?
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, when Zhi came to Huaqing Palace for his performance review, Yang Guozhong resented his ability and said to Remonstrance Officer Wu Zhizhi, "Can you expose Zhi's crimes?

sentences.zh: 吾以御史相處。」

translations.literal: I will treat you as a Censor.
translations.idiomatic: I will see to it that you are appointed a Censor.

sentences.zh: 豸之乃劾陟饋遺事，國忠又使甥婿韋元誌左驗，陟惶悸，賄吉溫求救，由是俱得罪，陟貶桂嶺尉，坐不行，徙平樂。

translations.literal: Zhizhi then impeached Zhi for bribery; Guozhong also had his nephew-in-law Wei Yuanzhi corroborate from the side; Zhi, terrified, bribed Ji Wen for rescue — thereby both fell into guilt; Zhi was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Guiling; for failing to go, he was transferred to Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi then impeached Zhi for giving gifts and bribes. Guozhong also had his nephew-in-law Wei Yuanzhi provide corroborating testimony. Zhi, in terror, bribed Ji Wen to plead for him, and thereby both men fell into guilt. Zhi was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Guiling; when he failed to take up the post, he was transferred to Pingle.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山陷洛陽，弟斌沒賊，國忠欲構陟與賊通，密諭守吏，令脅陟使憂死，州豪傑共說曰：「昔張說被竄，匿陳氏以免。

translations.literal: When An Lushan captured Luoyang, Zhi's younger brother Bin fell into rebel hands; Guozhong wished to frame Zhi for communicating with the rebels and secretly instructed the guarding officials to coerce Zhi into dying of grief; the leading men of the prefecture jointly urged him, saying: "In former times, when Zhang Yue was banished, he hid with the Chen clan to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured Luoyang, Zhi's younger brother Bin fell into rebel hands. Guozhong sought to frame Zhi for colluding with the rebels and secretly instructed the local officials to harass him until worry killed him. The leading men of the prefecture jointly urged him, saying, "In former times, when Zhang Yue was banished, he hid with the Chen clan and so escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 今若詔書下，誰敢庇公？

translations.literal: If an imperial edict is issued now, who would dare shelter you?
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial edict comes down now, who would dare shelter you?

sentences.zh: 願公乘扁舟遁去，事寧乃出，不亦美乎？」

translations.literal: We hope you will take a small boat and flee; when affairs are settled you can emerge — would that not be fine?
translations.idiomatic: We urge you to take a small boat and flee. When affairs are settled you can emerge again — would that not be best?

sentences.zh: 陟慨然曰：「命當爾，其敢逃刑？」

translations.literal: Zhi said with emotion: "If fate is thus, how would I dare flee punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said with feeling, "If this is what fate decrees, how would I dare flee punishment?"

sentences.zh: 因謝遣，堅臥不出。

translations.literal: He thereupon thanked them and sent them away, and lay abed steadfastly without going out.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked them and sent them away, then lay abed and steadfastly refused to go out.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，肅宗即位，起為吳郡太守，使者趣追，未至，會永王兵起，委陟招諭，乃授御史大夫、江東節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Emperor Suzong ascended the throne and recalled him as Administrator of Wu Commandery; envoys urgently summoned him, but before he arrived the Prince of Yong raised troops; he was entrusted to Zhi to summon and persuade, and he was then granted Censor-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, Emperor Suzong ascended the throne and recalled Zhi as Administrator of Wu Commandery. Envoys were sent to summon him urgently, but before he arrived the Prince of Yong raised troops. The court entrusted Zhi with the task of summoning and persuading the people, and appointed him Censor-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 與高適、來瑱會安州，陟曰：「今中原未平，江淮騷離，若不齋盟質信，以示四方，知吾等協心戮力，則無以成功。」

translations.literal: Meeting with Gao Shi and Lai Tian at Anzhou, Zhi said: "Now the Central Plains are not yet pacified and the Jianghuai region is in turmoil; if we do not purify ourselves and covenant in sincerity and trust to show the four quarters that we are united in heart and effort, we cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When he met with Gao Shi and Lai Tian at Anzhou, Zhi said, "The Central Plains are not yet pacified and the Jianghuai region is in turmoil. Unless we purify ourselves and swear a covenant of sincerity and trust, showing the four quarters that we are united in heart and effort, we cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 乃推瑱為地主，為載書，登壇曰：「淮西節度使瑱、江東節度使陟、淮南節度使適，銜國威命，糾合三垂，翦除兇慝，好惡同之，毋有異志。

translations.literal: He thereupon proposed Tian as host of the covenant, drew up the written oath, and ascending the altar said: "Military Commissioner of Huai West Tian, Military Commissioner of Jiangdong Zhi, and Military Commissioner of Huainan Shi, bearing the august mandate of the state, rallying the three frontier regions, cutting down violent evil — let our likes and dislikes be one, and let none harbor a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon proposed Tian as host of the covenant, drew up the written oath, and ascending the altar declared, "Military Commissioner of Huai West Tian, Military Commissioner of Jiangdong Zhi, and Military Commissioner of Huainan Shi, bearing the august mandate of the state, rallying the three frontier regions and cutting down violent evil — let our likes and dislikes be one, and let none harbor a different intent.

sentences.zh: 有渝此盟，墜命亡族，罔克生育。

translations.literal: Whoever violates this covenant — may he lose his life and destroy his clan, and may he not survive to bear offspring.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever violates this covenant — may he lose his life and destroy his clan, and may he not survive to bear offspring.

sentences.zh: 皇天後土，祖宗明神，實鑒斯言。」

translations.literal: Heaven above and Earth below, the bright spirits of our ancestors — truly witness these words."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven above and Earth below, and the bright spirits of our ancestors — bear witness to these words."

sentences.zh: 辭旨慷慨，士皆隕泣。

translations.literal: The words were impassioned in tone, and the officers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: His words were impassioned, and the officers all wept.

sentences.zh: 永王敗，帝趣陟赴鳳翔。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yong was defeated, the Emperor urged Zhi to go to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Yong was defeated, the Emperor urgently summoned Zhi to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 初，季廣琛從永王亂，非其本謀，陟表廣琛為歷陽太守，尉安之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji Guangchen had followed the Prince of Yong in rebellion, though it was not his original intent; Zhi memorialized to appoint Guangchen as Administrator of Liyang and reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ji Guangchen had followed the Prince of Yong in rebellion, though that had not been his original intent. Zhi memorialized to appoint Guangchen Administrator of Liyang and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 至是，恐廣琛有後變，乃馳往諭詔恩釋其疑，而後趣召。

translations.literal: At this time, fearing Guangchen might later turn against him, he galloped there to explain the imperial grace and dispel his suspicions, and only then urged him to report for summons.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, fearing Guangchen might later turn against him, he rode posthaste to explain the imperial grace and dispel his suspicions, and only then urged him to answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 帝雅聞陟名，欲倚以相，及是遷延，疑有顧望意，止除御史大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long admired Zhi's name and wished to rely on him as chief minister; but when he delayed arrival, the Emperor suspected wavering intent and only appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long admired Zhi's reputation and wished to rely on him as chief minister, but when Zhi delayed his arrival the Emperor suspected hesitation and appointed him only Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會杜甫論房琯，詞意迂慢，帝令陟與崔光遠、顏真卿按之，陟奏：「甫言雖狂，不失諫臣體。」

translations.literal: When Du Fu spoke on Fang Guan's behalf in language that was circuitous and disrespectful, the Emperor ordered Zhi, together with Cui Guangyuan and Yan Zhenqing, to investigate; Zhi memorialized: "Though Fu's words were wild, they did not fall short of the bearing proper to a remonstrating official.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fu spoke on Fang Guan's behalf in language that was circuitous and disrespectful, the Emperor ordered Zhi, together with Cui Guangyuan and Yan Zhenqing, to investigate the matter. Zhi memorialized, "Though Fu's words were wild, they did not fall short of the bearing proper to a remonstrating official.

sentences.zh: 帝繇是疏之。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor therefore kept Zhi at a distance.

sentences.zh: 富平人將軍王去榮殺其縣令，帝將宥之，陟曰：「昔漢高帝約法，殺人者死。

translations.literal: Wang Qurong, a general of Fuping, killed his county magistrate; the Emperor was about to pardon him; Zhi said: "In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han established the law: one who kills shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qurong, a general of Fuping, killed his county magistrate. When the Emperor was about to pardon him, Zhi said, "In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han established the law: one who kills shall die.

sentences.zh: 今陛下殺人者生，恐非所宜。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty would let one who kills live — I fear this is not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty would let a killer live — I fear this is not appropriate.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷尚新，群臣班殿中，有相吊哭者，帝以陟不任職，用顏真卿代之，更拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The court was still newly established; among the ministers arrayed in the hall some wept and mourned for one another; the Emperor considered Zhi unfit for office, replaced him with Yan Zhenqing, and reappointed him Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The court was still newly established, and among the ministers arrayed in the hall some wept and mourned for one another. The Emperor considered Zhi unfit for office, replaced him with Yan Zhenqing, and reappointed Zhi Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 久之，宗人伐墓柏，坐不相教，貶絳州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time, clansmen felled cypress at the tomb; for failing to restrain them he was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, clansmen felled cypress trees at the family tomb. For failing to restrain them, he was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還授太常卿，呂諲入輔，薦為禮部尚書、東京留守。

translations.literal: He was restored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; when Lu Yin entered as chief assistant, he recommended him as Minister of Rites and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to the post of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. When Lu Yin entered government as chief assistant, he recommended Zhi as Minister of Rites and Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 史思明逼伊、洛，李光弼議守河陽，陟率東京安屬入關避之，詔授吏部尚書，令就保永樂，以圖收復。

translations.literal: Shi Siming pressed toward Yi and Luo; Li Guangbi advocated holding Heyang; Zhi led the officials and dependents of the Eastern Capital into the passes to flee; he was ordered appointed Minister of Personnel and told to hold Yongle while planning reconquest.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming pressed toward the Yi and Luo region, Li Guangbi advocated holding Heyang. Zhi led the officials and dependents of the Eastern Capital into the passes to escape the threat. He was ordered appointed Minister of Personnel and instructed to hold Yongle while planning reconquest.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈荊州大都督。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously awarded Grand Protector General of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five and was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Protector General of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 陟早有名，而為林甫、國忠擯廢。

translations.literal: Zhi had early fame but was cast aside by Linfu and Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had won early renown, but was cast aside by Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 及肅宗擇相，自謂必得，以後至不用。

translations.literal: When Suzong chose a chief minister, he expected surely to obtain it — but because he arrived late, he was not used.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong chose a chief minister, Zhi expected surely to be appointed — but because he arrived late, he was passed over.

sentences.zh: 任事者皆新進，望風憚之，多言其驕倨。

translations.literal: Those in charge were all newly risen; at the sight of him they feared him, and many spoke of his arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Those then in office were all newly risen men who feared him at sight, and many spoke of his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 及入關，又不許至京師。

translations.literal: When he entered the passes, he was again not permitted to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the passes, he was again not permitted to reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 郁郁不得誌，成疾，且卒，嘆曰：「吾道窮於此乎！」

translations.literal: Depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions, he fell ill; as he was about to die he sighed: "Has my path come to an end here!
translations.idiomatic: Depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions, he fell ill. As death approached he sighed, "Has my path come to an end here!

sentences.zh: 性侈縱，喜飾服馬，侍兒閹童列左右常數十，侔於王宮主第。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and unrestrained, fond of adorning his dress and horses; maidservants and eunuch boys lined his left and right, often numbering several tens — rivaling princely palaces and noble estates.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant and unrestrained, fond of adorning his dress and horses. Maidservants and eunuch boys lined his left and right, often numbering several dozen — a household rivaling princely palaces and noble estates.

sentences.zh: 窮治饌羞，擇膏腴地藝谷麥，以鳥羽擇米，每食視庖中所棄，其直猶不減萬錢，宴公侯家，雖極水陸，曾不下箸。

translations.literal: He exhaustively prepared delicacies, selected fertile land to grow grain and wheat, sifted rice with bird feathers — each meal, looking at what the kitchen discarded, its value still did not fall below ten thousand cash; when feasting at the homes of dukes and marquises, though land and sea delicacies were at their utmost, he never once picked up his chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: He exhaustively prepared delicacies, selected fertile land on which to grow grain and wheat, and sifted rice with bird feathers. At each meal, the food discarded from his kitchen was still worth no less than ten thousand cash. When dining at the homes of dukes and marquises, though land and sea delicacies were laid out in full splendor, he never once picked up his chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 常以五采箋為書記，使侍妾主之，以裁答，受意而已，皆有楷法，陟唯署名，自謂所書「陟」字若五朵雲，時人慕之，號「郇公五雲體」。

translations.literal: He often used five-colored letter paper for correspondence, had maidservants manage it, and dictated replies — receiving his intent only — all in standard script; Zhi signed his name alone, saying the character "Zhi" that he wrote was like five clouds; people of the time admired it and called it "the Duke of Xun's Five-Cloud Script."
translations.idiomatic: He often used five-colored letter paper for his correspondence and had maidservants manage it, dictating replies from his intent alone — all in proper standard script. Zhi signed only his name, declaring that the character "Zhi" in his hand looked like five clouds. People of the time admired it and called it "the Duke of Xun's Five-Cloud Script."

sentences.zh: 然家法脩整，敕子允就學，夜分視之，見其勤，旦日問安，色必怡；

translations.literal: Yet household rules were strictly maintained: he ordered his son Yun to study; at midnight he inspected him — when he saw him diligent, the next morning when Yun asked after his health his expression was always pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his household rules were strictly maintained. He ordered his son Yun to study, and at midnight he would inspect him. When he found him diligent, his expression the next morning when Yun came to greet him was always pleased;

sentences.zh: 稍怠則立堂下不與語。

translations.literal: if Yun slackened even slightly, he would stand below the hall and not speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: if Yun slackened even slightly, Zhi would stand below the hall and refuse to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 雖家僮數十，然應門賓客，必允主之。

translations.literal: Though household servants numbered several tens, receiving guests at the door was always Yun's responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Though household servants numbered several dozen, receiving guests at the door was always Yun's responsibility.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, he was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, he was posthumously granted the title of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太常博士程皓議謚「忠孝」，顏真卿以為許國養親不兩立，不當合二行為謚，主客員外郎歸崇敬亦駁正之。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Doctor Cheng Hao proposed the posthumous name "Loyal and Filial"; Yan Zhenqing held that serving the state and supporting parents could not both be honored in one posthumous name, and that the two virtues ought not be combined in a single epithet; Principal Secretary for Guests Yuan Guichong also refuted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Doctor Cheng Hao proposed the posthumous name "Loyal and Filial." Yan Zhenqing held that serving the state and supporting one's parents could not both be honored in a single posthumous name, and that the two virtues ought not be combined in one epithet. Principal Secretary for Guests Guichong also refuted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 右僕射郭英乂無學術，卒用太常議云。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Guo Yingyi lacked learning, and in the end the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness' proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Guo Yingyi lacked scholarly learning, and in the end the proposal of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was adopted.

sentences.zh: 子 斌斌，父為相時授太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: Son Bin — Bin: when his father was chief minister he was granted Attendant in the Crown Prince's Secretariat for Communication of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin — Bin: when his father was chief minister he was granted the post of Attendant in the Crown Prince's Secretariat for Communication of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 少脩整，好文藝，容止嚴峭，有大臣體，與陟齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he was cultivated and orderly, fond of literature and the arts; his bearing was stern and austere, with the mien of a great minister — he was equally renowned with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was cultivated and orderly, fond of literature and the arts. His bearing was stern and austere, with the mien of a great minister, and he was equally renowned with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 開元中，薛王業以女妻之，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, Prince of Xue Ye gave him his daughter in marriage, and he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, the Prince of Xue, Ye, gave him his daughter in marriage, and he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，為中書舍人，兼集賢院學士，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he served as Attendant Drafting Scribe and concurrently as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then was changed to Vice Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he served as Attendant Drafting Scribe and concurrently as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then was transferred to Vice Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 李林甫構韋堅獄，斌以宗累，貶巴陵太守，移臨汝。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu fabricated the Wei Jian case, Bin was implicated by clan connection and demoted to Administrator of Baling, then transferred to Linru.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu fabricated the Wei Jian case, Bin was implicated through clan connection and demoted to Administrator of Baling, then transferred to Linru.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜銀青光祿大夫，列五品。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and ranked in the fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, ranking in the fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 時陟守河東，而從兄由為右金吾衛將軍，絳為太子少師，四第同時列戟，衣冠罕比者。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi was Administrator of Hedong, while his older cousin of the same generation You was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and Jiang was Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince — four households simultaneously displayed halberds at their gates, a rarity among officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhi was Administrator of Hedong, his older cousin of the same generation You was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and Jiang was Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. Four households of the clan simultaneously displayed halberds at their gates — a distinction rarely matched among officials.

sentences.zh: 祿山陷洛陽，斌為賊得，署以黃門侍郎，憂憤卒。

translations.literal: When Lushan captured Luoyang, Bin fell into rebel hands and was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; he died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan captured Luoyang, Bin fell into rebel hands and was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat. He died of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 斌天性質厚，每朝會，不敢離立笑言。

translations.literal: Bin was plain and solid by nature; at every court assembly he did not dare leave his place to stand apart and laugh or talk.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was plain and solid by nature. At every court assembly he never dared leave his place to stand apart and laugh or talk.

sentences.zh: 嘗大雪，在廷者皆振裾更立，斌不徙足，雪甚，幾至靴，亦不失恭。

translations.literal: Once during heavy snow, those in attendance all shook their robes and shifted where they stood; Bin did not move his feet — the snow piled deep, nearly reaching his boots, yet he never lost his reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Once during heavy snow, those in attendance all shook their robes and shifted where they stood. Bin did not move his feet. The snow piled deep, nearly reaching his boots, yet he never lost his reverence.

sentences.zh: 斌子 況子況，少隱王屋山，孔述睿稱之，及述睿以諫議大夫召，薦況為右拾遺，不拜。

translations.literal: Bin's son Kuang — Kuang: in youth he lived in seclusion on Mount Wangwu; Kong Shurui praised him; when Shurui was summoned as Remonstrance Officer, he recommended Kuang as Right Remonstrance Officer — Kuang declined.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's son Kuang — Kuang: in youth he lived in seclusion on Mount Wangwu. Kong Shurui praised him, and when Shurui was summoned as Remonstrance Officer he recommended Kuang for the post of Right Remonstrance Officer. Kuang declined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以起居郎召，半歲，輒棄官去，徙家龍門。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Attendant for Imperial Diaries; after half a year he abruptly resigned his office and left, moving his household to Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Attendant for Imperial Diaries, but after half a year he abruptly resigned and left office, moving his household to Longmen.

sentences.zh: 除司封員外郎，稱疾固辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Principal Secretary for Enfeoffment, but pleaded illness and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Principal Secretary for Enfeoffment, but pleaded illness and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 元和初，授諫議大夫，勉諭到職，數月，乞骸骨，以太子左庶子致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he was granted Remonstrance Officer; after earnest urging he took office; after several months he requested retirement; he retired as Left Mentor of the Crown Prince and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he was granted the post of Remonstrance Officer. After earnest urging he took office, but after several months he requested retirement. He retired as Left Mentor of the Crown Prince and later died.

sentences.zh: 況雖世貴，而誌沖遠，不為聲利所遷，當時重其風操。

translations.literal: Though Kuang came from an illustrious family, his aspiration was lofty and distant, and he was not swayed by fame and profit — people of the time respected his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Kuang came from an illustrious family, his aspirations were lofty and far-reaching, and he was not swayed by fame or profit. People of the time respected his integrity.

sentences.zh: 兄 叔夏叔夏，安石兄。

translations.literal: Elder brother Shuxia — Shuxia, Anshi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Shuxia — Shuxia was Anshi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 通禮家學。

translations.literal: He mastered the family's learning in rites.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the family's learning in rites.

sentences.zh: 叔父太子詹事琨嘗曰：「而能繼漢丞相業矣。」

translations.literal: His uncle, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Kun, once said: "You can continue the career of a Han dynasty chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Kun, once said, "You can continue the career of a Han dynasty chief minister.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，歷太常博士。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and served successively as Doctor of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and served successively as Doctor of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，恤禮亡缺，叔夏與中書舍人賈大隱、博士裴守真禋定其制，擢春官員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, mourning rites were lost and deficient; Shuxia, together with Attendant Drafting Scribe Jia Dayin and Doctor Pei Shouzhen, determined the ritual regulations for suburban and ancestral rites, and he was promoted to Principal Secretary of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong died, mourning rites were lost and deficient. Shuxia, together with Attendant Drafting Scribe Jia Dayin and Doctor Pei Shouzhen, determined the ritual regulations for suburban and ancestral rites, and he was promoted to Principal Secretary of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武後拜治，享明堂，凡所沿改，皆叔夏、祝欽明、郭山惲等所裁討。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu performed the feng and shan rites and offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall, all alterations and reforms were deliberated and researched by Shuxia, Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu performed the feng and shan rites and offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall, all alterations and reforms were deliberated and researched by Shuxia, Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, and others.

sentences.zh: 每立一議，眾咨服之。

translations.literal: Whenever he established a proposal, the multitude consulted and submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he established a proposal, the assembled scholars consulted and submitted to it.

sentences.zh: 累遷成均司業。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：「五禮儀物，司禮博士有所脩革，須叔夏、欽明等評處，然後以聞。」

translations.literal: Later an edict also stated: "For ritual implements of the Five Rites, whenever Doctors of Rites revise or alter them, Shuxia, Qinming, and others must evaluate and decide before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict also stated, "For ritual implements of the Five Rites, whenever Doctors of Rites revise or alter them, Shuxia, Qinming, and others must evaluate and decide before reporting to the throne.

sentences.zh: 進位春官侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to the post of Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，轉太常少卿，為建立廟社使，進銀青光祿大夫，累封沛郡公，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was restored to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, made Commissioner for Establishing the Ancestral Temple and Altars of Soil and Grain, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, successively enfeoffed as Duke of Pei Commandery, and appointed Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was restored to the throne, Shuxia was transferred to Vice Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and made Commissioner for Establishing the Ancestral Temple and Altars of Soil and Grain. He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, successively enfeoffed as Duke of Pei Commandery, and appointed Rector of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州都督、脩文館學士，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Protector General of Yanzhou and Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature; his posthumous name was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the titles of Protector General of Yanzhou and Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature. His posthumous name was Wen.

sentences.zh: 子縚。

translations.literal: His son was Chao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chao.

sentences.zh: 叔夏子 抗縚，開元時歷集賢修撰、光祿卿，遷太常。

translations.literal: Shuxia's son Chao — during the Kaiyuan era he successively served as Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Director of Imperial Banquets, and was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxia's son Chao — during the Kaiyuan era he successively served as Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Director of Imperial Banquets, and was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 唐興，禮文雖具，然制度時時繆缺不倫。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, ritual texts though complete, yet institutions were from time to time erroneous, deficient, and inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty arose, ritual texts were complete in form, yet institutions were from time to time erroneous, deficient, and inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 至顯慶中，許敬宗建言：「籩豆以多為貴，宗廟乃旂於天，請大祀十二、中祀十、小祀八。

translations.literal: By the Xianqing era, Xu Jingzong proposed: "For bian and dou vessels, abundance is prized; the ancestral temple is a banner toward Heaven — I request great sacrifices twelve, medium sacrifices ten, small sacrifices eight.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xianqing era, Xu Jingzong proposed, "For bian and dou vessels, abundance is prized, and the ancestral temple is a banner toward Heaven. I request twelve for great sacrifices, ten for medium sacrifices, and eight for small sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大祀、中祀、簠、簋、鉶、俎皆一，小祀無鉶。」

translations.literal: For great, medium, and small sacrifices — fu, gui, xing, and zu vessels each one; small sacrifices have no xing.
translations.idiomatic: For great, medium, and small sacrifices, the fu, gui, xing, and zu vessels should each be one set; small sacrifices would have no xing.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，赦令以籩豆之薦，未能備物，宜詔禮官學士共議以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an amnesty edict stated that offerings in bian and dou vessels had not yet been fully supplied with implements, and that ritual officials and scholars should jointly deliberate and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, an amnesty edict stated that offerings in bian and dou vessels had not yet been fully supplied with implements, and ordered ritual officials and scholars to deliberate jointly and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 縚請「宗廟籩豆皆加十二。」

translations.literal: Chao requested: "For the ancestral temple, all bian and dou vessels should be increased to twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Chao requested, "For the ancestral temple, all bian and dou vessels should be increased to twelve.

sentences.zh: 又言「郊奠，爵容止一合，容小則陋，宜增大之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "For suburban offerings, the wine vessel holds only one he — too small appears shabby; it should be enlarged."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "For suburban offerings, the wine vessel holds only one he — too small appears shabby, and it should be enlarged."

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎張均、職方郎中韋述議曰：「《禮》：『天之所生，地之所長，茍可薦者，莫不鹹在。』

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Bureau Director of Appointments Wei Shu debated, saying: "The 《Rites》 states: 'What Heaven produces and Earth brings forth — if it can be offered, none is not all present.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Bureau Director of Appointments Wei Shu debated, saying, "The 《Rites》 states, 'What Heaven produces and Earth brings forth — if it can be offered, none is not all present.

sentences.zh: 聖人知孝子之情深，而物類無限，故為之節，使物有品，器有數，貴賤差降，不得相越。

translations.literal: The sage knew that a filial son's feeling runs deep, yet the kinds of things are limitless — therefore he set bounds, so that things have grades, vessels have numbers, high and low differ in descent, and none may overstep.
translations.idiomatic: The sage knew that a filial son's feeling runs deep, yet the kinds of things are limitless. Therefore he set bounds, so that things have grades, vessels have numbers, high and low differ in rank, and none may overstep.

sentences.zh: 周制：王，食用六谷，膳用六牲，飲用六清，羞用百有二十品，珍用八物，醬用百有二十甕，而以四籩、四豆供祭祀。

translations.literal: Zhou institutions: for the king, food used six grains, meals used six sacrificial animals, drink used six clear liquids, delicacies used one hundred and twenty kinds, rare foods used eight items, sauces used one hundred and twenty jars — yet only four bian and four dou were used to supply sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou institutions, the king's food used six grains, his meals six sacrificial animals, his drink six clear liquids, his delicacies one hundred and twenty kinds, his rare foods eight items, and his sauces one hundred and twenty jars — yet only four bian and four dou were used to supply sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 此祀與賓客豐省不得同，舊矣。

translations.literal: That sacrificial offerings and guest entertainment differ in abundance and restraint is an old principle.
translations.idiomatic: That sacrificial offerings and guest entertainment differ in abundance and restraint is an old principle.

sentences.zh: 且嗜好燕私之饌，與時而遷，故聖人一約以禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, favored foods for private feasting shift with the times — therefore the sage unified all under ritual bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, favored foods for private feasting shift with the times, and therefore the sage unified all under the bounds of ritual.

sentences.zh: 雖平生所嗜，非禮則不薦；

translations.literal: Even what one loved throughout life — if not according to ritual, it is not offered;
translations.idiomatic: Even what one loved throughout life is not offered if it falls outside ritual;

sentences.zh: 所惡，是禮則不去。

translations.literal: what one hated — if ritual requires it, it is not removed.
translations.idiomatic: and what one hated is not removed if ritual requires it.

sentences.zh: 屈建命去祥祭之芰曰：『祭典有之，不羞珍異，不陳庶侈。』

translations.literal: Qu Jian ordered the removal of water caltrop from the auspicious sacrifice, saying: 'The sacrificial canon has it: do not offer rare delicacies, do not display miscellaneous luxuries.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jian ordered water caltrop removed from the auspicious sacrifice, saying, "The sacrificial canon states, 'Do not offer rare delicacies; do not display miscellaneous luxuries.

sentences.zh: 此則禮外之食，前古不薦。

translations.literal: This is food outside ritual — ancient times did not offer it.
translations.idiomatic: This is food outside ritual, and ancient times did not offer it.

sentences.zh: 今欲以甘旨肥濃皆充於祭，茍逾舊制，其何極焉。

translations.literal: Now if you wish to fill the sacrifice entirely with sweet delicacies and rich, fatty foods, and if it exceeds the old regulations, where would be the limit?
translations.idiomatic: If one now wishes to fill the sacrifice with every sweet delicacy and rich, fatty food, and that exceeds the old regulations, there would be no limit.

sentences.zh: 雖籩豆有加，不能備也。

translations.literal: Even if bian and dou vessels are increased, they cannot be made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the bian and dou vessels are increased, they still cannot be fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 若曰以今之珍，生所嗜愛，求神無方，是簠、簋可去，而盤、盂、杯、案當禦矣；

translations.literal: If one says that because today's delicacies were what the deceased loved in life, and seeking the spirits has no fixed method, then fu and gui could be removed and plates, bowls, cups, and trays should be used instead;
translations.idiomatic: If one argues that today's delicacies were what the deceased loved in life and that there is no fixed way to seek the spirits, then fu and gui could be discarded and plates, bowls, cups, and trays ought to be used instead;

sentences.zh: 韶、瑀可抵，而箜篌、笙、笛應奏矣。

translations.literal: Shao and yu regalia could be replaced, and konghou, sheng, and flutes should be played.
translations.idiomatic: the Shao and yu regalia could be set aside, and konghou, sheng, and flutes ought to be performed.

sentences.zh: 且自漢以來，陵有寢宮，歲時朔望，薦以常饌，固可盡孝子之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Han times tombs have had sleeping palaces; at the seasonal new and full moons, regular meals are offered — this can indeed fulfill a filial son's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Han times tombs have had sleeping palaces where regular meals are offered at the seasonal new and full moons, and that can indeed fulfill a filial son's heart.

sentences.zh: 至宗廟法享，不可變古從俗。

translations.literal: As for statutory offerings in the ancestral temple, one cannot change the ancient way to follow custom.
translations.idiomatic: But statutory offerings in the ancestral temple cannot be altered from ancient practice to follow custom.

sentences.zh: 有司所承，一升爵，五升散。

translations.literal: What the officials carry out is one sheng in the jue and five sheng in the san.
translations.idiomatic: What the officials carry out is one sheng in the jue and five sheng in the san.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：凡宗廟，貴者以爵，賤者以散，此貴小賤大，以示節儉。

translations.literal: The 《Rites》: for ancestral temples generally, the noble use the jue and the lowly use the san — this honors the small and demeans the great, to show frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 states that in ancestral temples generally, the noble use the jue and the lowly use the san — honoring the small and demeaning the great to show frugality.

sentences.zh: 請如故。」

translations.literal: We request that it remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that matters remain as before."

sentences.zh: 太子賓客崔沔曰：「古者，有所飲食，必先嚴獻，未化火，則有毛血之薦，未麹糵，則有玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: Chief Mentor to the Crown Prince Cui Mian said: "In antiquity, whenever there was food or drink, one first made a strict offering; before fire had transformed it, there was the offering of raw flesh and blood; before malt had been prepared, there was the presentation of dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Mentor to the Crown Prince Cui Mian said, "In antiquity, whenever there was food or drink, one first made a strict offering. Before fire had transformed it, raw flesh and blood were offered; before malt had been prepared, dark wine was presented.

sentences.zh: 至後王，作酒醴、用犧牲，故有三牲、八簋、五齊、九獻。

translations.literal: Later kings made wine and ale and used sacrificial animals, and therefore there came to be the three sacrificial animals, eight gui, five grades of wine, and nine presentations.
translations.idiomatic: Later kings made wine and ale and used sacrificial animals, and so there came to be the three sacrificial animals, eight gui, five grades of wine, and nine presentations.

sentences.zh: 然神尚玄，可存而不可測也；

translations.literal: Yet spirits esteem the mysterious — it can be preserved but cannot be measured;
translations.idiomatic: Yet spirits esteem the mysterious, which can be preserved but cannot be measured;

sentences.zh: 祭主敬，可備而不可廢也。

translations.literal: sacrifice values reverence — it can be prepared but cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: and sacrifice values reverence, which can be prepared but cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 蓋薦貴新，味不尚褻，雖曰備物，猶有節制存焉。

translations.literal: Offerings value freshness; flavor does not esteem the profane — even though one speaks of complete offerings, restraint still remains.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings value freshness, and flavor does not esteem the profane. Even when one speaks of complete offerings, restraint still remains.

sentences.zh: 铏、俎、籩、豆、簠、簋、尊、罍，周人時饌也，其用通於燕享賓客，周公乃與毛血玄酒共薦。

translations.literal: Xing, zu, bian, dou, fu, gui, zun, and lei — these were the Zhou people's seasonal foods; their use extended to banquets and entertaining guests, and the Duke of Zhou then offered them together with raw blood and dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, zu, bian, dou, fu, gui, zun, and lei were the Zhou people's seasonal foods. Their use extended to banquets and entertaining guests, and the Duke of Zhou then offered them together with raw blood and dark wine.

sentences.zh: 晉中郎盧諶家祭，皆晉日食，則當時之食，不可闕於祀已。

translations.literal: In Jin, Palace Attendant Lu Chen's family sacrifices all used Jin daily fare — then the food of the time cannot be omitted from sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Palace Attendant Lu Chen's family sacrifices all used the daily fare of Jin, so the food of the time cannot be omitted from sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 唐家清廟時享，禮饌備進，周法也；

translations.literal: The Tang family's seasonal offerings in the Clear Temple, with ritual foods fully presented — that is the Zhou method;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang court's seasonal offerings in the Clear Temple, with ritual foods fully presented, follow the Zhou method;

sentences.zh: 園寢上食，時膳具陳，漢法也。

translations.literal: upper offerings at the garden tomb, with seasonal meals fully laid out — that is the Han method.
translations.idiomatic: while upper offerings at the garden tomb, with seasonal meals fully laid out, follow the Han method.

sentences.zh: 職貢助祭，致遠物也；

translations.literal: Official tribute assisting sacrifice presents goods from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Official tribute assisting sacrifice presents goods from afar;

sentences.zh: 有新必薦，順時令也。

translations.literal: when there is something new, it must be offered — this follows the seasonal command.
translations.idiomatic: when there is something new, it must be offered, following the seasonal command.

sentences.zh: 苑囿躬稼所入，搜田親發所中，皆因宜以薦，薦而後食。

translations.literal: What enters from produce personally farmed in the imperial parks, and what is taken in hunts personally conducted — all are offered as appropriate, and only after offering does one eat.
translations.idiomatic: What enters from produce personally farmed in the imperial parks and what is taken in hunts personally conducted are all offered as appropriate, and only after offering does one eat.

sentences.zh: 則濃腴鮮美盡在矣。

translations.literal: Then rich, fatty, fresh, and delicious things are all there.
translations.idiomatic: In that way, rich, fatty, fresh, and delicious things are all included.

sentences.zh: 又敕有司著於令，不必加籩豆之數也。

translations.literal: Moreover, order the officials to record this in regulations — there is no need to increase the number of bian and dou vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the officials should be ordered to record this in regulations, without increasing the number of bian and dou vessels.

sentences.zh: 大凡祭器，視物所宜。

translations.literal: Generally, sacrificial vessels depend on what suits the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, sacrificial vessels depend on what suits the offering.

sentences.zh: 故大羹，古饌也，盛以鉶，鉶，古器也；

translations.literal: Thus great soup is ancient fare, served in a xing — the xing is an ancient vessel;
translations.idiomatic: Thus great soup is ancient fare, served in a xing, which is an ancient vessel;

sentences.zh: 和羹，時饌也，盛以铏，铏，時器也。

translations.literal: seasoned soup is contemporary fare, served in a xing — the xing is a contemporary vessel.
translations.idiomatic: while seasoned soup is contemporary fare, served in a xing, which is a contemporary vessel.

sentences.zh: 有古饌而用時器者，則毛血於盤，玄酒於尊。

translations.literal: When there is ancient fare but contemporary vessels are used, then raw blood is placed on a plate and dark wine in a zun.
translations.idiomatic: When there is ancient fare but contemporary vessels are used, raw blood is placed on a plate and dark wine in a zun.

sentences.zh: 未有進時饌用古器者，古質而今文，有所不稱也。

translations.literal: There has never been a case of presenting contemporary fare in ancient vessels — ancient substance with contemporary ornamentation; something does not match.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been a case of presenting contemporary fare in ancient vessels — ancient substance with contemporary ornamentation is ill-suited.

sentences.zh: 雖加籩豆十二，未足盡天下之美，而措諸廟，徒以近侈而見訾柢。

translations.literal: Even if twelve bian and dou are added, it is not enough to exhaust the world's beauties, and placing them in the temple merely invites blame for recent extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Even adding twelve bian and dou would not exhaust the world's beauties, and placing them in the temple would merely invite blame for recent extravagance.

sentences.zh: 臣聞墨家者流，出於清廟，是廟貴儉不尚奢也。」

translations.literal: I have heard that the Mohist school arose from the Clear Temple — the temple values frugality and does not esteem luxury."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Mohist school arose from the Clear Temple, where the temple values frugality and does not esteem luxury.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎楊仲昌、戶部郎中陽伯成、左衛兵曹參軍劉秩等，請如舊禮便。

translations.literal: Deputy Director of the Ministry of Rites Yang Zhongchang, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng, Military Officer of the Left Guard Liu Zhi, and others requested that the old ritual be followed for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Director of the Ministry of Rites Yang Zhongchang, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng, Military Officer of the Left Guard Liu Zhi, and others asked that the old ritual be followed.

sentences.zh: 宰相白奏，玄宗曰：「朕承祖宗休德，享祀粢盛，實貴豐潔。

translations.literal: The chancellor reported this, and Emperor Xuanzong said: "I inherit my ancestors' excellent virtue; in enjoying sacrifice with full grain offerings, I truly value abundance and purity.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor reported this, and Emperor Xuanzong said, "I inherit my ancestors' excellent virtue, and in enjoying sacrifice with full grain offerings, I truly value abundance and purity.

sentences.zh: 有如不應於法，亦不敢用。」

translations.literal: If something does not accord with the law, I also dare not use it."
translations.idiomatic: If something does not accord with the law, I also dare not use it.

sentences.zh: 乃詔太常，擇品味可增者稍加焉。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to select flavors that could be increased and add to them slightly.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to select flavors that could be increased and add to them slightly.

sentences.zh: 縚又請室加籩、豆各六，每四時以新果珍饔實之。

translations.literal: Chao again requested that each chamber add six bian and six dou each, filled each season with fresh fruits and fine delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Chao again requested that each chamber add six bian and six dou each, filled each season with fresh fruits and fine delicacies.

sentences.zh: 制「可」。

translations.literal: An edict read: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「獻爵視藥升所容，以合古。」

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The capacity of the offering cup should follow the capacity of the standard sheng measure, to accord with antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated, "The capacity of the offering cup should follow the capacity of the standard sheng measure, to accord with antiquity."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，詔書服紀所未通者，令禮官學士詳議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an edict stated that where mourning dress regulations were not yet clear, ritual officials and scholars were to discuss them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, an edict stated that where mourning dress regulations were not yet clear, ritual officials and scholars were to discuss them in detail.

sentences.zh: 縚上言：「《禮》《喪服》：舅，緦麻三月。

translations.literal: Chao submitted: "The 《Rites》 and 《Mourning Dress》: for an uncle, si ma for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Chao submitted, "The 《Rites》 and 《Mourning Dress》 prescribe si ma for three months for an uncle.

sentences.zh: 從母，小功五月，《傳》曰：『何以小功，以名加也。』

translations.literal: For a mother's sister, xiao gong for five months. The 《Commentary》 says: 'Why xiao gong? Because the name is added.
translations.idiomatic: For a mother's sister, xiao gong for five months. The 《Commentary》 asks, "Why xiao gong? Because the name is added."

sentences.zh: 而堂姨、舅母，恩所不及焉。

translations.literal: Yet for a paternal hall aunt and an uncle's wife, affection does not reach that far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a paternal hall aunt and an uncle's wife, affection does not reach that far.

sentences.zh: 外祖父母，小功五月，《傳》曰：『何以小功，以尊加也。』

translations.literal: For maternal grandparents, xiao gong for five months. The 《Commentary》 says: 'Why xiao gong? Because respect is added.
translations.idiomatic: For maternal grandparents, xiao gong for five months. The 《Commentary》 asks, "Why xiao gong? Because respect is added."

sentences.zh: 舅，緦麻三月，皆情親而屬疏也。

translations.literal: For an uncle, si ma for three months — all are emotionally close yet affiliation is distant.
translations.idiomatic: For an uncle, si ma for three months — all are emotionally close yet affiliation is distant.

sentences.zh: 外祖正尊，服同從母；

translations.literal: Maternal grandparents are proper elders, and the dress is the same as for a mother's sister;
translations.idiomatic: Maternal grandparents are proper elders, and the mourning dress is the same as for a mother's sister;

sentences.zh: 姨、舅一等，而有輕重；

translations.literal: aunt and uncle are of one rank, yet there are heavy and light differences;
translations.idiomatic: aunt and uncle are of one rank, yet the mourning grades differ in weight;

sentences.zh: 堂姨、舅親未疏，不相為服；

translations.literal: a paternal hall aunt and uncle — kinship is not distant, yet they do not wear mourning for one another;
translations.idiomatic: for a paternal hall aunt and uncle, kinship is not distant, yet they do not wear mourning for one another;

sentences.zh: 親舅母不如同爨。

translations.literal: one's own uncle's wife is regarded less than a same-hearth kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: and one's own uncle's wife is regarded less than a same-hearth kinsman.

sentences.zh: 其亦古意有所未暢。

translations.literal: This also shows that the ancient meaning had something not fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: This also shows that the ancient meaning had something not fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 且外祖小功，此為正尊，請進至大功；

translations.literal: Moreover, maternal grandparents wear xiao gong — this is for proper elders; we request advancing it to da gong;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, maternal grandparents wear xiao gong, and as proper elders they should be advanced to da gong;

sentences.zh: 姨、舅儕親，服宜等，請進舅至小功；

translations.literal: aunt and uncle are peer kin — the dress should be equal; we request advancing an uncle to xiao gong;
translations.idiomatic: aunt and uncle are peer kin, so the dress should be equal, and we request advancing an uncle to xiao gong;

sentences.zh: 堂姨舅以疏降親舅從母一等；

translations.literal: a paternal hall aunt and uncle, because of distant descent, should be one grade below one's own uncle and mother's sister;
translations.idiomatic: a paternal hall aunt and uncle, because of distant descent, should be one grade below one's own uncle and mother's sister;

sentences.zh: 親舅母古未有服，請從袒免。」

translations.literal: for one's own uncle's wife, antiquity had no mourning dress — we request following tan mian."
translations.idiomatic: for one's own uncle's wife, antiquity prescribed no mourning dress, and we request following tan mian."

sentences.zh: 於是韋述議曰：「自高祖至玄孫並身謂之九族。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei Shu debated, saying: "From the great-great-grandfather down to the great-great-great-grandson, all in one body are called the nine clans.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wei Shu debated, saying, "From the great-great-grandfather down to the great-great-great-grandson, all in one body are called the nine clans.

sentences.zh: 由近及遠，差其輕重，遂為五服。

translations.literal: From near to far, their weight is differentiated, and thus there are the five mourning grades.
translations.idiomatic: From near to far, their weight is differentiated, and thus there are the five mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『外親服皆緦。』

translations.literal: The 《Commentary》 says: 'Mourning dress for external kin is all si.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Commentary》 states, "Mourning dress for external kin is all si."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：『外親之服異姓，正服不過緦。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: 'Mourning dress for external kin is of a different surname; proper dress does not exceed si.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said, "Mourning dress for external kin is of a different surname; proper dress does not exceed si."

sentences.zh: 外祖父母小功，以尊加；

translations.literal: Maternal grandparents wear xiao gong because respect is added;
translations.idiomatic: Maternal grandparents wear xiao gong because respect is added;

sentences.zh: 從母小功，以名加；

translations.literal: a mother's sister wears xiao gong because the name is added;
translations.idiomatic: a mother's sister wears xiao gong because the name is added;

sentences.zh: 舅、甥、外孫、中外昆弟，皆緦。

translations.literal: uncle, nephew by marriage, external grandson, and inner-outer brothers all wear si.
