translations.idiomatic: uncle, nephew by marriage, external grandson, and inner-outer brothers all wear si.

sentences.zh: 以匹言之，外祖則祖也，舅則伯叔也，父母之恩不殊，而獨殺於外者有以也。

translations.literal: Speaking as peers, a maternal grandparent is a grandparent and an uncle is an uncle — the grace of parents is not different, yet mourning alone is reduced for external kin; there is reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking as peers, a maternal grandparent is a grandparent and an uncle is an uncle. The grace of parents is not different, yet mourning alone is reduced for external kin, and there is reason for this.

sentences.zh: 禽獸知母而不知父，野人則父母等，都邑之士則知尊禰，大夫則知尊祖，諸侯及太祖，天子及始祖。

translations.literal: Beasts know the mother but not the father; wild people treat parents equally; town gentry know to honor the father; great officers know to honor the grandfather; feudal lords honor the great ancestor; the Son of Heaven honors the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts know the mother but not the father; wild people treat parents equally; town gentry know to honor the father; great officers know to honor the grandfather; feudal lords honor the great ancestor; and the Son of Heaven honors the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 聖人究天道，厚祖禰，系姓族，親子孫，則母黨之於本族，不同明甚。

translations.literal: The sage investigates Heaven's way, thickly honors ancestors, ties together surname clans, and cherishes descendants — then the mother's kin in relation to the root clan is clearly not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The sage investigates Heaven's way, thickly honors ancestors, ties together surname clans, and cherishes descendants, so the mother's kin in relation to the root clan is clearly not the same.

sentences.zh: 家無二尊，喪無二斬，人之所奉，不可貳也。

translations.literal: A household has no two elders; mourning has no two zhan — what people revere cannot be duplicated.
translations.idiomatic: A household has no two elders, and mourning has no two zhan — what people revere cannot be duplicated.

sentences.zh: 為人後，降其父母喪。

translations.literal: One who becomes an heir reduces mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: One who becomes an heir reduces mourning for his parents.

sentences.zh: 女子嫁，殺其家之喪。

translations.literal: When a woman marries, she reduces mourning for her family's kin.
translations.idiomatic: When a woman marries, she reduces mourning for her family's kin.

sentences.zh: 所存者遠，抑者私也。

translations.literal: What is preserved is the distant; what is suppressed is the private.
translations.idiomatic: What is preserved is the distant, and what is suppressed is the private.

sentences.zh: 若外祖及舅加一等，而堂舅及姨著服，則中外其別幾何？

translations.literal: If maternal grandparents and an uncle are raised one grade, and a paternal hall aunt and uncle receive mourning dress, then how much difference remains between inner and outer kin?
translations.idiomatic: If maternal grandparents and an uncle are raised one grade, and a paternal hall aunt and uncle receive mourning dress, then how much difference remains between inner and outer kin?

sentences.zh: 且五服有上殺之義，伯叔父母服大功，從父昆弟亦大功，以其出於祖，服不得過於祖也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the five mourning grades have the principle of upward reduction: an uncle's parents wear da gong, and father's brothers also wear da gong, because they derive from the grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the five mourning grades have the principle of upward reduction: an uncle's parents wear da gong, and father's brothers also wear da gong, because they derive from the grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the grandfather.

sentences.zh: 從祖祖父母、從祖父母、從祖昆弟皆小功，以其出於曾祖，服不得過曾祖也。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather's grandfather, great-grandfather's grandmother, and great-grandfather's brothers all wear xiao gong, because they derive from the great-grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the great-grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather's grandfather, great-grandfather's grandmother, and great-grandfather's brothers all wear xiao gong, because they derive from the great-grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the great-grandfather.

sentences.zh: 族祖祖父母、族祖父母、族昆弟皆緦，以其出於高祖，服不得過高祖也。

translations.literal: Clan great-grandfathers, clan great-grandmothers, and clan brothers all wear si, because they derive from the great-great-grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the great-great-grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Clan great-grandfathers, clan great-grandmothers, and clan brothers all wear si, because they derive from the great-great-grandfather and mourning cannot exceed that for the great-great-grandfather.

sentences.zh: 堂姨、舅出外曾祖，若為之服，則外曾祖父母、外伯叔祖父母亦可制服矣。

translations.literal: A paternal hall aunt and uncle derive from the external great-grandfather — if mourning dress is worn for them, then external great-grandparents and external uncle-grandparents could also receive mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: A paternal hall aunt and uncle derive from the external great-grandfather. If mourning dress is worn for them, then external great-grandparents and external uncle-grandparents could also receive mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 外祖至大功，則外曾祖小功、外高祖緦。

translations.literal: If maternal grandparents are advanced to da gong, then external great-grandparents would wear xiao gong and the external great-great-grandfather would wear si.
translations.idiomatic: If maternal grandparents are advanced to da gong, then external great-grandparents would wear xiao gong and the external great-great-grandfather would wear si.

sentences.zh: 推而廣之，與本族無異。

translations.literal: Extend this broadly, and there is no difference from the root clan.
translations.idiomatic: Extend this broadly, and there is no difference from the root clan.

sentences.zh: 棄親錄疏，不可謂順。

translations.literal: To abandon the close and record the distant cannot be called obedience.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the close and record the distant cannot be called obedience.

sentences.zh: 且服皆有報，則堂甥、外曾孫、侄女之子皆當服。

translations.literal: Moreover, mourning dress always has reciprocity — then a hall nephew, an external great-grandson, and a niece's sons should all wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, mourning dress always has reciprocity, so a hall nephew, an external great-grandson, and a niece's sons should all wear mourning.

sentences.zh: 聖人豈薄其骨肉恩愛哉？

translations.literal: Did the sage slight flesh-and-blood affection?
translations.idiomatic: Did the sage slight flesh-and-blood affection?

sentences.zh: 盡本於公者末於私，義有所斷，不得不然。

translations.literal: To exhaust oneself in the public and end in the private — righteousness has its breaks, and one cannot but be so.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust oneself in the public and end in the private — righteousness has its breaks, and one must be so.

sentences.zh: 茍可加也，則可減也，如是，禮可隳矣。

translations.literal: If it can be increased, then it can be reduced; if so, ritual can be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If mourning can be increased, then it can be reduced, and in that case ritual can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 請如古便。」

translations.literal: We request following the ancient custom."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the ancient custom be followed."

sentences.zh: 楊仲昌又言：「舅服小功，魏徵嘗進之矣。

translations.literal: Yang Zhongchang again said: "Mourning dress for an uncle at xiao gong — Wei Zheng once proposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongchang again said, "Mourning dress for an uncle at xiao gong was once proposed by Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 今之所請，正同徵論。

translations.literal: What is requested today is exactly the same as Zheng's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The present request matches Zheng's argument exactly.

sentences.zh: 堂舅、堂姨、舅母，皆升袒免，則外祖父母進至大功，不加報於外孫乎？

translations.literal: A paternal hall uncle, paternal hall aunt, and uncle's wife are all raised to tan mian — then are maternal grandparents advanced to da gong without adding reciprocity for an external grandson?
translations.idiomatic: If a paternal hall uncle, paternal hall aunt, and uncle's wife are all raised to tan mian, then are maternal grandparents advanced to da gong without adding reciprocity for an external grandson?

sentences.zh: 外孫而報以大功，則本宗之庶孫用何等邪？」

translations.literal: If an external grandson reciprocates with da gong, then what grade is used for a common grandson of the root clan?"
translations.idiomatic: If an external grandson reciprocates with da gong, then what grade is used for a common grandson of the root clan?"

sentences.zh: 帝手敕曰：「朕謂親姨、舅服小功，則舅母於舅有三年之喪，不得全降於舅，宜服緦。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote by hand: "I hold that for one's own aunt and uncle the dress should be xiao gong — then for an uncle's wife, who has three years' mourning for her husband, she cannot fully reduce mourning for her husband and should wear si.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote by hand, "I hold that for one's own aunt and uncle the dress should be xiao gong. Then for an uncle's wife, who has three years' mourning for her husband, she cannot fully reduce mourning for her husband and should wear si.

sentences.zh: 堂姨、舅古未有服，朕思睦厚九族，宜袒免。

translations.literal: For a paternal hall aunt and uncle, antiquity had no mourning dress — I think to harmonize and thicken the nine clans, tan mian is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: For a paternal hall aunt and uncle, antiquity had no mourning dress. I think that to harmonize and thicken the nine clans, tan mian is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 古有同爨緦，若比堂姨、舅於同爨，不已厚乎？

translations.literal: Antiquity had si ma for same-hearth kin — if one compares a paternal hall aunt and uncle to same-hearth kin, is that not already generous?
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had si ma for same-hearth kin. If one compares a paternal hall aunt and uncle to same-hearth kin, is that not already generous?

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『外親服皆緦。』

translations.literal: The 《Commentary》 says: 'Mourning dress for external kin is all si.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Commentary》 states, "Mourning dress for external kin is all si."

sentences.zh: 是亦不隔堂姨、舅也。

translations.literal: This also does not exclude a paternal hall aunt and uncle.
translations.idiomatic: This also does not exclude a paternal hall aunt and uncle.

sentences.zh: 若謂所服不得過本，而復為外曾祖父母、外伯叔父母制服，亦何傷？

translations.literal: If one says mourning dress cannot exceed that for one's root clan, yet one again wears mourning for external great-grandparents and external uncle-grandparents — what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: If one says mourning dress cannot exceed that for one's root clan, yet one again wears mourning for external great-grandparents and external uncle-grandparents, what harm is there?

sentences.zh: 皆親親敦本意也。」

translations.literal: All of this cherishes kin and thickens the original intent."
translations.idiomatic: All of this cherishes kin and thickens the original intent."

sentences.zh: 侍中裴耀卿、中書令張九齡、禮部尚書李林甫奏言：「外服無降，甥為舅母服，舅母亦報之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief Pei Yaoqing, Palace Secretary Zhang Jiuling, and Minister of the Ministry of Rites Li Linfu memorialized, saying: "External mourning dress has no reduction — a nephew wears mourning for his uncle's wife, and the uncle's wife also reciprocates.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-chief Pei Yaoqing, Palace Secretary Zhang Jiuling, and Minister of the Ministry of Rites Li Linfu memorialized, saying, "External mourning dress has no reduction. A nephew wears mourning for his uncle's wife, and the uncle's wife also reciprocates.

sentences.zh: 夫之甥既報，則夫之姨、舅又當服，恐所引益疏。

translations.literal: If the husband's nephew already reciprocates, then the husband's maternal aunt and maternal uncle should again wear mourning — we fear those cited grow ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: If the husband's nephew already reciprocates in mourning, then the husband's maternal aunt and uncle must also be mourned, and we fear the kin cited grow ever more remote.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚，皆所不及。」

translations.literal: We your ministers are dull; all of this is beyond us."
translations.idiomatic: We are too dull to grasp these matters fully."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「從服六，此其一也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Derived mourning is six; this is one of them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "There are six types of derived mourning dress; this is one of them.

sentences.zh: 降殺於禮無文，皆自身率親為之數。

translations.literal: Reduction in mourning grade has no written rule in ritual — all are numbers derived from oneself leading kin.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual provides no written rule for reducing mourning grades; each case is reckoned from the degree owed to one's own close kin.

sentences.zh: 姨、舅屬近，以親言之，亦姑伯之匹，可曰所引疏耶？

translations.literal: Maternal aunt and maternal uncle are near kin; speaking in terms of closeness, they are peers of paternal aunt and elder uncle — can one say those cited are distant?
translations.idiomatic: A maternal aunt and uncle are close kin; in degree of relationship they match a paternal aunt and uncle. How can one call such kin remote?

sentences.zh: 婦人從夫者也，夫於姨舅既服矣，從夫而服，是謂睦親。

translations.literal: A woman follows her husband; the husband already wears mourning for maternal aunt and uncle — following the husband in mourning is called drawing kin close.
translations.idiomatic: A wife follows her husband. If the husband already mourns his wife's maternal aunt and uncle, for her to follow him in mourning is what draws the families together.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜熟計。」

translations.literal: You ministers should consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: You should weigh this matter carefully."

sentences.zh: 耀卿等奏言：「舅母緦，堂姨舅袒免。

translations.literal: Yaoqing and others memorialized, saying: "For an uncle's wife, three-month sí mourning; for hall maternal aunt and uncle, bared shoulder and uncapped head.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqing and the others memorialized, saying, "An uncle's wife warrants three-month sí mourning; a hall maternal aunt and uncle warrant bared-shoulder and uncapped-head mourning.

sentences.zh: 請準制旨，自我為古，罷諸儒議。」

translations.literal: We ask to follow the imperial decree, take the present as antiquity, and end the various Confucian debates."
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow Your Majesty's decree, establish the present rule as precedent, and end further scholarly debate."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 初，帝詔歲率公卿迎氣東郊，至三時，常以孟月讀《時令》於正寢。

translations.literal: Initially, the Emperor decreed that each year he would lead dukes and ministers to welcome the qi at the eastern suburb; by the third season, they regularly in the first month of each season read the Seasonal Ordinances in the main quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Emperor decreed that each year he would lead the chief ministers to welcome the seasonal qi at the eastern suburb. By the third season, they regularly read the Seasonal Ordinances in the first month of each season in the main palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，詔縚月奏《令》一篇，朔日於宣政側設榻，東向置案，縚坐讀之，諸司官長悉升殿坐聽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict ordered Tao to present monthly one chapter of the Ordinances; on the first day of the month a couch was set beside Xuanzheng, a desk placed facing east, Tao sat and read it, and the heads of all departments ascended the hall and sat to listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict required Pei Tao to recite one chapter of the Ordinances each month. On the first day of the month a couch was placed beside the Xuanzheng Hall with an east-facing desk; Tao sat and read aloud while the heads of every department ascended the hall to listen.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，罷。

translations.literal: After a year and more, it was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, the practice was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 高宗上元三年，將袷享。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan under Emperor Gaozong, a xia offering was about to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Shangyuan era under Emperor Gaozong, the court was preparing to perform a xia sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 議者以《禮緯》三年袷，五年禘；

translations.literal: Those debating cited the Ritual Apocrypha: xia in the third year, di in the fifth year;
translations.idiomatic: Debaters cited the Ritual Apocrypha, which says xia in the third year and di in the fifth;

sentences.zh: 《公羊》家五年再殷祭。

translations.literal: the Gongyang school held two grand offerings in five years.
translations.idiomatic: while the Gongyang school held two grand offerings within five years.

sentences.zh: 二家舛互，諸儒莫能決。

translations.literal: The two schools contradicted one another, and the scholars could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The two traditions contradicted each other, and none of the scholars could settle the question.

sentences.zh: 太學博士史玄璨曰：「《春秋》：僖公三十三年十二月薨。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial University Shi Xuancan said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals records: Duke Xi died in the twelfth month of his thirty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuancan, erudite of the Imperial University, said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals records that Duke Xi of Lu died in the twelfth month of his thirty-third year.

sentences.zh: 文公之二年八月丁卯，大享。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duke Wen, on the day dingmao of the eighth month, a great offering was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duke Wen, on the dingmao day of the eighth month, a great offering was performed.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》曰：『袷也。』

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: 'It was a xia offering.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says, 'This was a xia sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 則三年喪畢，新君之二年當袷，明年當禘群廟。

translations.literal: Then when the three-year mourning was complete, in the new ruler's second year there should be xia, and the next year di for all the temples.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, once the three-year mourning was complete, the new ruler's second year should see xia, and the following year di for all the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 又宣公八年，禘僖公。

translations.literal: Again, in Duke Xuan's eighth year, di was performed for Duke Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in Duke Xuan's eighth year, di was performed for Duke Xi.

sentences.zh: 宣公八年皆有禘，則後禘距前禘五年。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan's eighth year had di in both cases, so the later di was five years from the earlier di.
translations.idiomatic: Since di was performed in Duke Xuan's eighth year in both instances, the later di came five years after the earlier one.

sentences.zh: 此則新君之二年袷、三年禘爾。

translations.literal: This was simply xia in the new ruler's second year and di in the third.
translations.idiomatic: This means xia in the new ruler's second year and di in the third.

sentences.zh: 後五年再殷祭，則六年當袷，八年禘。

translations.literal: After five years came two grand offerings again, so in the sixth year there should be xia and in the eighth di.
translations.idiomatic: After five years came two grand offerings again, so the sixth year should see xia and the eighth di.

sentences.zh: 昭公十年，齊歸薨。

translations.literal: In Duke Zhao's tenth year, Lady Qi Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Zhao's tenth year, Lady Qi Gui died.

sentences.zh: 十三年，喪畢當袷，為平丘之會。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when mourning was complete xia was due, but there was the meeting at Pingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when mourning was complete and xia was due, the meeting at Pingqiu intervened.

sentences.zh: 冬，公如晉，至十四年袷，十五年禘。

translations.literal: In winter the Duke went to Jin; xia came in the fourteenth year and di in the fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Duke went to Jin; xia was performed in the fourteenth year and di in the fifteenth.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰『有事於武宮』是也。

translations.literal: The Commentary says 'there were affairs at the Wu Palace' — this is that case.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary's line 'there were affairs at the Wu Palace' refers to this.

sentences.zh: 至十八年袷，二十年禘；

translations.literal: Then xia in the eighteenth year and di in the twentieth;
translations.idiomatic: Then came xia in the eighteenth year and di in the twentieth;

sentences.zh: 二十三年袷，二十五年禘。

translations.literal: xia in the twenty-third year and di in the twenty-fifth.
translations.idiomatic: xia in the twenty-third year and di in the twenty-fifth.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十五年『有事於襄宮』是也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's twenty-fifth year, 'there were affairs at the Xiang Palace' — this is that case.
translations.idiomatic: The line in Duke Zhao's twenty-fifth year, 'there were affairs at the Xiang Palace,' refers to this.

sentences.zh: 則禘後三年而袷，又二年而禘，合於禮。」

translations.literal: Thus after di, three years then xia, and two years later di — this accords with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Thus after di came xia three years later, and di again two years after that — in accord with ritual."

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The debate was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the debate was settled.

sentences.zh: 後睿宗喪畢，袷於廟。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Ruizong's mourning was complete, xia was performed at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Ruizong's mourning period ended, xia was performed at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 至開元二十七年，禘祭五，袷祭七。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan, there had been five di sacrifices and seven xia sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan, the court had performed five di sacrifices and seven xia sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是歲，縚奏：「四月嘗已禘，孟冬又袷，祀禮叢數，請以夏禘為大祭之源。」

translations.literal: That year Tao memorialized: "In the fourth month the seasonal offering had already been di, and in early winter there was xia again — sacrificial rites are piled in number; we ask to take the summer di as the source of the great offering."
translations.idiomatic: That year Pei Tao memorialized, "Di had already been performed at the fourth-month offering, and xia was held again in early winter. Sacrifices had become too numerous; he asked that the summer di be treated as the basis for the grand offering."

sentences.zh: 自是相循，五年再祭矣。

translations.literal: From then on this was followed, and two offerings came every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this practice was followed, and two offerings were held every five years.

sentences.zh: 縚終太子少師。

translations.literal: Tao ended as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tao ended his career as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子 抗抗者，安石從父兄子。

translations.literal: Son of a paternal cousin: Kang. Kang was the son of Wei Anshi's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, son of a paternal cousin: he was the son of Wei Anshi's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉明經，累官吏部郎中。

translations.literal: At weak-crown he passed the Mingjing examination and rose through offices to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At age twenty he passed the Mingjing examination and rose through the ranks to become a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，為永昌令，輦轂繁要，抗不事威刑而治，前令無及者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he served as magistrate of Yongchang; the capital region was busy and vital — Kang did not rely on harsh punishments yet governed well, and no previous magistrate matched him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingyun era he served as magistrate of Yongchang. The capital district was crowded and demanding, yet Kang governed without relying on harsh punishments, and no previous magistrate had matched him.

sentences.zh: 遷右御史臺中丞，邑民詣闕留，不聽，乃立碑著其惠。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right Censorate; the district people went to the palace to petition that he stay, but this was not granted, so they erected a stele recording his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the Right Censorate. The people of his district petitioned at the palace to keep him, but the request was denied, so they erected a stele recording his beneficence.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，自太子左庶子為益州大都督府長兄，授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, from Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent he became chief secretary of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate and was awarded the post of Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan he moved from Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent to chief secretary of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate and was concurrently appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 河曲胡康待賓叛，詔持節慰撫。

translations.literal: The Hu chieftain Kang Daibin of the river bend rebelled; an edict ordered Kang to go bearing credentials to console and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Daibin, a Hu leader of the river bend, rebelled, and an edict ordered Wei Kang to go as imperial commissioner to console and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 抗於武略非所長，稱疾逗留，不及賊而返。

translations.literal: Kang was not skilled in military affairs; he claimed illness and lingered, failed to reach the rebels, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Military strategy was not Kang's strength. He pleaded illness and delayed, failed to reach the rebels, and returned.

sentences.zh: 俄代王晙為御史大夫，兼按察京畿。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Jun as Censor-in-chief and concurrently inspected the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he replaced Wang Jun as censor-in-chief and concurrently served as inspector of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 弟拯方為萬年令，兄弟領本部，時以為榮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zheng was then magistrate of Wannian; the brothers both held posts in the same jurisdiction, and the age regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zheng was then magistrate of Wannian, so the brothers both held office in the same jurisdiction — a distinction widely admired at the time.

sentences.zh: 坐薦御史非其人，授安州都督，改蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: He was punished for recommending an unfit person as censor, was appointed Protector-General of Anzhou, and was changed to Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for recommending the wrong man as censor, appointed Protector-General of Anzhou, and then transferred to serve as prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，進刑部尚書，分掌吏部選，卒。

translations.literal: He entered court as Chief Minister of Justice, advanced to Minister of Punishments, shared charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as chief minister of justice, rose to Minister of Punishments, shared responsibility for personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 抗歷職以清儉，不治產，及終無以葬，玄宗聞之，特給槥車。

translations.literal: Kang throughout his offices was pure and frugal, did not build up property, and at death had no means for burial; Emperor Xuanzong heard of this and specially granted a hearse.
translations.idiomatic: Kang served with integrity and frugality, amassed no estate, and at his death had no means for burial. When Emperor Xuanzong learned of this, he specially provided a hearse.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 所表奉天尉梁升卿、新豐尉王倕、華原尉王燾，皆為僚屬，後皆為顯人。

translations.literal: Those he recommended — Fengtian Assistant Magistrate Liang Shengqing, Xinfeng Assistant Magistrate Wang Wei, and Huayuan Assistant Magistrate Wang Tao — all became his subordinates, and later all became eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: The men he recommended — Liang Shengqing, assistant magistrate of Fengtian; Wang Wei, assistant magistrate of Xinfeng; and Wang Tao, assistant magistrate of Huayuan — all became his subordinates and later rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 升卿涉學工書，於八分尤工，歷廣州都督，書《東封朝覲碑》，為時絕筆。

translations.literal: Shengqing was broadly learned and skilled in calligraphy, especially masterful in clerical script; he served as Protector-General of Guangzhou and wrote the Stele of the Eastern Feng and Court Audience — a supreme brushwork of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shengqing was broadly learned and skilled in calligraphy, especially in clerical script. He later served as Protector-General of Guangzhou and wrote the Stele of the Eastern Feng and Court Audience, a masterpiece of his age.

sentences.zh: 倕累遷河西節度使，天寶中，功聞於邊。

translations.literal: Wei rose through posts to Military Commissioner of Hexi; in the Tianbao era his achievements were known on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wei rose through the ranks to become military commissioner of Hexi, and during the Tianbao era his achievements were renowned on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 它所辟舉，如王維、王縉、崔殷等，皆一時選雲。

translations.literal: Others he recruited and recommended, such as Wang Wei, Wang Ji, and Cui Yin, were all outstanding selections of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Others he recruited and promoted, such as Wang Wei, Wang Ji, and Cui Yin, were all outstanding men of the age.

sentences.zh: 郭震，字元振，魏州貴鄉人，以字顯。

translations.literal: Guo Zhen, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou, known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhen, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou and was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，美須髯，少有大誌。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet tall, with handsome beard and whiskers, and from youth had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, with a fine beard, and from youth harbored great ambition.

sentences.zh: 十六，與薛稷、趙彥昭同為太學生，家嘗送資錢四十萬，會有缞服者叩門，自言「五世未葬，願假以治喪」。

translations.literal: At sixteen, together with Xue Ji and Zhao Yanzhao he was a student at the Imperial University; his family once sent him four hundred thousand in funds, when a man in hemp mourning knocked at the door, saying himself, "Five generations have gone unburied — I wish to borrow this to arrange funerals."
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he studied at the Imperial University alongside Xue Ji and Zhao Yanzhao. His family once sent him four hundred thousand cash in support, when a man in mourning clothes knocked at the door and said, "Five generations of my family lie unburied. I beg to borrow this money to arrange their funerals."

sentences.zh: 元振舉與之，無少吝，一不質名氏。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen lifted it and gave it to him, without the least stinginess, and never asked his name.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen gave him the entire sum without the least hesitation and never asked his name.

sentences.zh: 稷等嘆駭。

translations.literal: Ji and the others sighed in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and the others were astonished.

sentences.zh: 十八舉進士，為通泉尉。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination and became assistant magistrate of Tongquan.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Tongquan.

sentences.zh: 任俠使氣，撥去小節，嘗盜鑄及掠賣部中口千餘，以餉遺賓客，百姓厭苦。

translations.literal: He was chivalrous and bold in spirit, set aside minor scruples, once illicitly cast coins and seized and sold more than a thousand people in the district to supply and entertain guests — the common people were weary and afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and chivalrous, cared little for minor scruples, and once illicitly cast coins and seized and sold more than a thousand people in his district to entertain guests. The common people suffered greatly under him.

sentences.zh: 武後知所為，召欲詰，既與語，奇之，索所為文章，上《寶劍篇》，後覽嘉嘆，詔示學士李嶠等，即授右武衛鎧曹參軍，進奉宸監丞。

translations.literal: Empress Wu learned what he had done, summoned him intending to interrogate him, but after speaking with him was struck by him, asked for writings he had composed, and he presented the "Ode on the Precious Sword"; the Empress read it, praised and sighed, ordered it shown to Academician Li Jiao and others, and immediately appointed him Army-Armor Staff Officer of the Right Martial Guard, advancing to Director of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu learned what he had done, she summoned him to question him. After speaking with him she was impressed, asked for his writings, and he presented his Ode on the Precious Sword. The Empress read it with admiration, had it shown to Academician Li Jiao and others, and immediately appointed him army-armor staff officer in the Right Martial Guard, then promoted him to director of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃乞和，其大將論欽陵請罷四鎮兵，披十姓之地，乃以元振充使，因覘虜情。

translations.literal: It happened that Tibet sought peace; its great general Lun Qinling asked to disband the Four Garrisons' troops and open the lands of the Ten Surnames — Yuanzhen was then appointed envoy to observe the barbarians' disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet sought peace, its great general Lun Qinling asked that the Four Garrisons be disbanded and the lands of the Ten Surnames be opened. Yuanzhen was appointed envoy so he could observe Tibetan intentions.

sentences.zh: 還，上疏曰：

translations.literal: On his return he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 利或生害，害亦生利。

translations.literal: Benefit may give rise to harm; harm may also give rise to benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Benefit can breed harm, and harm can also breed benefit.

sentences.zh: 國家所患，唯吐蕃與默啜耳，今皆和附，是將大利於中國也。

translations.literal: What the state fears is only Tibet and Mohe alone; now both have made peace and submitted — this will greatly benefit China.
translations.idiomatic: The state's chief threats have been Tibet and Mohe alone. Now both have submitted to peace — a great benefit to the empire.

sentences.zh: 若圖之不審，害且隨之。

translations.literal: If the plan is not considered carefully, harm will follow.
translations.idiomatic: If the policy is not weighed carefully, harm will follow.

sentences.zh: 欽陵欲裂十姓地，解四鎮兵，此動靜之機，不可輕也。

translations.literal: Qinling wishes to split off the lands of the Ten Surnames and disband the Four Garrisons' troops — this is a pivot of movement and stillness and cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Qinling wants to carve away the lands of the Ten Surnames and disband the Four Garrisons. This turning point must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 若直遏其意，恐邊患必甚於前，宜以策緩之，使其和望勿絕，而惡不得萌，固當取舍審也。

translations.literal: If we directly thwart his intent, I fear frontier troubles will surely exceed those before; we should use stratagem to ease matters, so that their hope for peace is not cut off yet evil cannot sprout — the choice must indeed be made with care.
translations.idiomatic: If we bluntly reject his proposal, frontier troubles may exceed those of the past. We should use strategy to stall him, keep their hopes for peace alive, and prevent trouble from taking root. The choice must be made with care.

sentences.zh: 夫患在外者，十姓、四鎮是也；

translations.literal: Now, troubles on the outside are the Ten Surnames and the Four Garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: External threats lie in the Ten Surnames and the Four Garrisons;

sentences.zh: 患在內者，甘、涼、瓜、肅是也。

translations.literal: troubles on the inside are Gan, Liang, Gua, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: internal troubles lie in Gan, Liang, Gua, and Su.

sentences.zh: 關隴屯戍，向三十年，力用困竭，脫甘、涼有一日警，豈堪廣調發耶？

translations.literal: Guan and Long have garrisoned troops for nearly thirty years; strength and resources are exhausted. If Gan and Liang should have one day's alarm, how could they bear broad mobilization?
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Long have maintained garrisons for nearly thirty years until strength and resources are exhausted. If Gan or Liang should face even a single day's alarm, how could the region bear a major mobilization?

sentences.zh: 善為國者，先料內以敵外，不貪外以害內，然後安平可保。

translations.literal: One who governs a state well first calculates the interior to meet the exterior, and does not covet the exterior to harm the interior — then peace and security can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: A state that is well governed first secures its interior to meet external threats and does not sacrifice the interior for external gain. Only then can peace and security be preserved.

sentences.zh: 欽陵以四鎮近己，畏我侵掠，此吐蕃之要；

translations.literal: Qinling, because the Four Garrisons are near him, fears our raids — this is Tibet's vital point;
translations.idiomatic: Qinling fears our raids because the Four Garrisons lie close to him. That is Tibet's vital concern;

sentences.zh: 然青海、吐渾密邇蘭、鄯，易為我患，亦國家之要。

translations.literal: yet Qinghai and Tuyuhun are close to Lan and Shan, easily becoming a trouble to us — this too is the state's vital point.
translations.idiomatic: yet Qinghai and Tuyuhun lie close to Lan and Shan and can easily become a threat to us. That is also a vital concern for the state.

sentences.zh: 今宜報欽陵曰：「四鎮本扼諸蕃走集，以分其力，使不得並兵東侵。

translations.literal: Now we should reply to Qinling, saying: "The Four Garrisons originally choked the routes where the various barbarians gather and flee, to divide their strength and keep them from combining armies to invade eastward.
translations.idiomatic: We should now reply to Qinling, saying, "The Four Garrisons were originally positioned to block the routes by which the various tribes gather, dividing their strength so they could not combine and invade eastward.

sentences.zh: 今委之，則番力益強，易以擾動，保後無東意，當以吐渾諸部、青海故地歸於我，則俟斤部落還吐蕃矣。」

translations.literal: If we now relinquish them, then barbarian strength will grow stronger and disturbance will come easily; to guarantee no eastern intent afterward, the various Tuyuhun tribes and the old lands of Qinghai should be returned to us — then the Irkin tribes would revert to Tibet."
translations.idiomatic: If we surrender them now, tribal strength will grow and unrest will come easily. To guarantee no future eastern aggression, the Tuyuhun tribes and the old Qinghai territories should be returned to us; only then would the Irkin tribes revert to Tibetan control."

sentences.zh: 此足杜欽陵口，而和議未絕。

translations.literal: This is enough to stop Qinling's mouth, yet the peace talks are not broken off.
translations.idiomatic: This would shut Qinling's mouth while keeping the peace talks alive.

sentences.zh: 且四鎮久附，其倚國之心，豈與吐蕃等？

translations.literal: Moreover, the Four Garrisons have long been attached; their hearts relying on the state — how could they equal Tibet?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Four Garrisons have long been loyal to us. How could their reliance on the state be the same as Tibet's?

sentences.zh: 今未知利害情實而分裂之，恐傷諸國意，非制禦之算。

translations.literal: Now, without knowing the true situation of benefit and harm, to split them apart — I fear this will wound the hearts of the various states; it is not a plan for control and defense.
translations.idiomatic: To partition them now without knowing the true balance of advantage and harm would likely alienate the various states and is no sound policy of control.

sentences.zh: 後從之。

translations.literal: Later the court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court later adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 又言：「吐蕃倦徭戍久矣，鹹願解和；

translations.literal: He also said: "Tibet has long been weary of corvée and garrison duty; all wish to make peace;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Tibet has long been weary of corvée and frontier garrison duty, and all wish for peace;

sentences.zh: 以欽陵欲裂四鎮，專制其國，故未歸款。

translations.literal: because Qinling wishes to split off the Four Garrisons and monopolize control of the state, they have therefore not submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: but because Qinling wants to carve away the Four Garrisons and dominate the realm, they have not yet submitted in earnest.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能歲發和親使，而欽陵常不從，則其下必怨，設欲大舉，固不能，斯離間之漸也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly send peace-and-kinship envoys every year, and Qinling regularly does not comply, then those below will surely resent him; even if he wished to launch a major campaign, he fundamentally could not — this is the gradual way to sow division."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends peace envoys every year and Qinling regularly refuses, his subordinates will surely resent him. Even if he wished to launch a major campaign, he could not — this is the gradual way to sow division."

sentences.zh: 後然其計。

translations.literal: Later they approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court later approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 後數年，吐蕃君臣相猜攜，卒誅欽陵，而其弟贊婆等來降，因詔元振與河源軍大使夫蒙令卿率騎往迎。

translations.literal: Several years later, Tibet's ruler and ministers mutually suspected and divided; Qinling was finally executed, and his younger brother Zanpo and others came to surrender — an edict then ordered Yuanzhen and the envoy of the Heyuan Army, Fumeng Lingqing, to lead cavalry to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, Tibet's ruler and ministers turned against one another. Qinling was finally executed, and his younger brother Zanpo and others surrendered. An edict ordered Yuanzhen and Fumeng Lingqing, envoy of the Heyuan Army, to lead cavalry to receive them.

sentences.zh: 授主客郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director in the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 久之，突厥、吐蕃聯兵寇涼州，後方禦洛城門宴，邊遽至，因輟樂，拜元振為涼州都督，即遣之。

translations.literal: After some time, Turks and Tibet joined forces to raid Liangzhou; Empress Wu was holding a banquet at the Luoyang city gate when the frontier alarm suddenly arrived — music was stopped, Yuanzhen was appointed Protector-General of Liangzhou, and he was immediately dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, Turks and Tibet joined forces to raid Liangzhou. Empress Wu was holding a banquet at the Luoyang city gate when urgent news arrived from the frontier. The music stopped, Yuanzhen was appointed Protector-General of Liangzhou, and he was sent off at once.

sentences.zh: 初，州境輪廣才四百里，虜來必傅城下。

translations.literal: Initially the prefecture's circumference was only four hundred li wide; when barbarians came they always pressed against the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefecture's territory extended only four hundred li in circumference, and whenever raiders came they pressed right up to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 元振始於南硤口置和戎城，北磧置白亭軍，制束要路，遂拓境千五百里，自是州無虜憂。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen first placed Hecheng Fort at the Southern Gorge Pass and Baiting Army in the northern desert, controlling the vital routes, and thus expanded the territory by one thousand five hundred li — from then on the prefecture had no barbarian worries.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen first built Hecheng Fort at the Southern Gorge Pass and established Baiting Army in the northern desert, controlling the vital routes. He expanded the territory by fifteen hundred li, and from then on the prefecture was free of barbarian threats.

sentences.zh: 又遣甘州刺史李漢通辟屯田，盡水陸之利，稻收豐衍。

translations.literal: He also sent Ganzhou Prefect Li Hantong to open military colonies, fully exploiting the benefits of water and land — the rice harvest was abundant and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Li Hantong, prefect of Ganzhou, to open military colonies and exploit every advantage of water and land. The rice harvest grew abundant.

sentences.zh: 舊涼州粟斛售數千，至是歲數登，至匹縑易數十斛，支廥十年，牛羊被野。

translations.literal: Formerly in Liangzhou a bushel of grain sold for several thousand; by this time harvests came year after year, until a bolt of silk traded for several tens of bushels — granaries sufficed for ten years, and cattle and sheep covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a bushel of grain in Liangzhou sold for several thousand cash. Now harvests came year after year, until a bolt of silk could buy several dozen bushels. Granaries held enough for ten years, and cattle and sheep covered the fields.

sentences.zh: 治涼五歲，善撫禦，夷夏畏慕，令行禁止，道不舉遺。

translations.literal: He governed Liang for five years, good at comforting and defending; barbarians and Chinese alike feared and admired him — orders went forth and prohibitions stood; nothing was picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Liangzhou for five years with skillful administration and defense. Barbarians and Chinese alike respected and admired him. His orders were obeyed, and nothing was left abandoned on the roads.

sentences.zh: 河西諸郡置生祠，揭碑頌德。

translations.literal: The various prefectures of Hexi set up living shrines to him and erected steles praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Hexi built living shrines to him and erected steles praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，遷左驍衛將軍、安西大都護。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was transferred to General of the Left Martial Courage Guard and Grand Protector of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was transferred to general of the Left Martial Courage Guard and Grand Protector of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 西突厥酋烏質勒部落盛強，款塞願和，元振即牙帳與計事。

translations.literal: The Western Turk chieftain Wuzhile's tribe was flourishing and strong; he came to the border seeking peace — Yuanzhen went straight to his royal tent to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk chieftain Wuzhile commanded a powerful tribe and came to the border seeking peace. Yuanzhen went directly to his royal tent to discuss affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，元振立不動，至夕凍冽；

translations.literal: It happened that heavy rain and snow fell; Yuanzhen stood without moving until evening, when he was frozen stiff;
translations.idiomatic: A heavy snowstorm came up. Yuanzhen stood without moving until evening, when he was frozen stiff;

sentences.zh: 烏質勒已老，數拜伏，不勝寒，會罷即死。

translations.literal: Wuzhile was already old; he bowed prostrate repeatedly, unable to bear the cold, and as soon as the meeting ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile was already old. He bowed prostrate again and again, unable to endure the cold, and died as soon as the meeting ended.

sentences.zh: 其子娑葛以元振計殺其父，謀勒兵襲擊，副使解琬知之，勸元振夜遁，元振不聽，堅臥營為不疑者。

translations.literal: His son Suoge believed Yuanzhen's scheme had killed his father and plotted to muster troops for a surprise attack. Vice-envoy Xie Wan learned of this and urged Yuanzhen to flee by night. Yuanzhen refused and lay firmly in camp as one who suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suoge believed Yuanzhen's scheme had killed his father and plotted to muster troops for a surprise attack. Vice-envoy Xie Wan learned of this and urged Yuanzhen to flee by night, but Yuanzhen refused and lay firmly in camp as though he suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 明日，素服往吊，道逢娑葛兵，虜不意元振來，遂不敢逼，揚言迎衛。

translations.literal: The next day, dressed in plain mourning garb, he went to offer condolences. On the road he met Suoge's troops. The barbarians had not expected Yuanzhen to come and therefore did not dare press him; they proclaimed they were coming to welcome and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, dressed in plain mourning garb, he went to offer condolences. On the road he met Suoge's troops. The barbarians had not expected Yuanzhen to come and did not dare press him; they proclaimed that they had come to welcome and escort him.

sentences.zh: 進至其帳，修吊贈禮，哭甚哀，為留數十日助喪事，娑葛感義，更遣使獻馬五千、駝二百、牛羊十餘萬。

translations.literal: He proceeded to his tent, performed the rites of mourning and condolence gifts, and wept very sorrowfully. He stayed several tens of days to assist with funeral affairs. Moved by his righteous conduct, Suoge again sent envoys to present five thousand horses, two hundred camels, and more than one hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to Suoge's tent, performed the rites of mourning and condolence gifts, and wept with deep sorrow. He remained several tens of days to assist with the funeral. Moved by his righteous conduct, Suoge again sent envoys presenting five thousand horses, two hundred camels, and more than one hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 制詔元振為金山道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: An imperial edict appointed Yuanzhen Grand Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict appointed Yuanzhen Grand Commander on Campaign of the Jinshan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 烏質勒之將闕啜忠節與娑葛交怨，屢相侵，而闕啜兵弱不支。

translations.literal: Wuzhile's general Quechuo Zhongjie and Suoge nursed mutual grudges and repeatedly attacked each other, but Quechuo's forces were weak and could not hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile's general Quechuo Zhongjie and Suoge nursed mutual grudges and repeatedly raided each other, but Quechuo's forces were too weak to hold their own.

sentences.zh: 元振奏請追闕啜入宿衛，徙部落置瓜、沙間。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen memorialized requesting that Quechuo be summoned to serve in the palace guard and that his tribes be relocated and settled between Guazhou and Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen memorialized requesting that Quechuo be summoned to serve in the palace guard and that his tribes be relocated and settled between Guazhou and Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved this by edict.

sentences.zh: 闕啜遂行。

translations.literal: Quechuo then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Quechuo then set out.

sentences.zh: 至播仙城，遇經略使周以悌，以悌說之曰：「國家厚秩待君，以部落有兵故也。

translations.literal: When he reached Boxian City he met the frontier commissioner Zhou Yiti, who persuaded him, saying: "The state treats you with generous rank and salary because your tribe has troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Boxian City he met the frontier commissioner Zhou Yiti, who persuaded him, saying, "The state treats you with generous rank and salary because your tribe has troops.

sentences.zh: 今獨行入朝，一矰旅胡人耳，何以自全？」

translations.literal: If you go to court alone now, you are merely a single arrow-flight of a barbarian — how can you preserve yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: If you go to court alone now, you are merely a lone barbarian traveler — how can you preserve yourself?"

sentences.zh: 乃教以重寶賂宰相，無入朝，請發安西兵導吐蕃以擊娑葛；

translations.literal: He then taught him to bribe the chief ministers with heavy treasures, not to enter court, and to request that Anxi troops be dispatched to lead Tibet in an attack on Suoge;
translations.idiomatic: He then taught him to bribe the chief ministers with heavy treasures, not to enter court, and to request that Anxi troops be dispatched to lead Tibet in an attack on Suoge;

sentences.zh: 求阿史那獻為可汗以招十姓；

translations.literal: to seek Ashina Xian as khan to win over the Ten Surnames;
translations.idiomatic: to seek Ashina Xian as khan to win over the Ten Surnames;

sentences.zh: 請郭虔瓘使拔汗那搜其鎧馬以助軍，既得復讎，部落更存。

translations.literal: and to request Guo Qianjin be sent to Bohuana to requisition their armor and horses to aid the army — once vengeance is achieved, the tribes would survive again.
translations.idiomatic: and to request that Guo Qianjin be sent to Ferghana to requisition armor and horses to aid the army — once vengeance was achieved, the tribes would survive.

sentences.zh: 闕啜然之，即勒兵擊於闐坎城，下之。

translations.literal: Quechuo agreed and immediately mustered troops to attack Yutian's Kan City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Quechuo agreed and immediately mustered troops to attack Kan City in Yutian and captured it.

sentences.zh: 因所獲，遣人間道賫黃金分遺宗楚客、紀處訥，使就其謀。

translations.literal: Using what he had captured, he sent men by secret routes bearing gold to distribute to Zong Chuke and Ji Chune, so that they might carry out his plot.
translations.idiomatic: Using what he had captured, he sent men by secret routes bearing gold to distribute among Zong Chuke and Ji Chune so that they might carry out his plot.

sentences.zh: 元振知之，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yuanzhen learned of this and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen learned of this and submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 國家往不與吐蕃十姓、四鎮而不擾邊者，蓋其諸豪泥婆羅等屬國自有攜貳，故贊普南征，身殞寇庭，國中大亂，嫡庶競立，將相爭權，自相翦屠，士畜疲癘，財力困窮，顧人事、天時兩不諧契，所以屈誌於漢，非實忘十姓、四鎮也。

translations.literal: In the past the state did not cede the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons to Tibet, yet the border was not disturbed — this was because its various chieftains and subject states such as Nepal had their own divided loyalties. Therefore when the tsenpo marched south, he perished in the enemy's territory; the state fell into great turmoil; legitimate and illegitimate sons competed for the throne; generals and ministers wrestled for power and slaughtered one another; men and livestock were worn out and sick; wealth and strength were exhausted. Considering that human affairs and heavenly timing were both out of accord, they therefore humbled their will before Han — not because they truly forgot the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the past the state did not cede the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons to Tibet, yet the frontier was not disturbed, because its various chieftains and subject states such as Nepal had their own divided loyalties. When the tsenpo marched south, he perished in enemy territory; the realm fell into great turmoil; legitimate and illegitimate sons competed for the throne; generals and ministers fought for power and slaughtered one another; men and livestock were exhausted and plague-stricken; resources were depleted. Human affairs and heavenly timing were both out of accord, so they humbled themselves before Han — not because they had truly forgotten the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 如其有力，後且必爭。

translations.literal: If they had strength, later they would surely contest them.
translations.idiomatic: If they had the strength, they would surely contest them later.

sentences.zh: 今忠節忽國家大計，欲為吐蕃鄉導主人，四鎮危機恐從此啟。

translations.literal: Now Zhongjie ignores the state's grand strategy and wishes to serve as Tibet's guide and master — the peril to the Four Garrisons may well begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhongjie ignores the state's grand strategy and wishes to serve as Tibet's guide and patron — the crisis threatening the Four Garrisons may well begin here.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃得誌，忠節亦當在賊掌股，若為復得事我哉？

translations.literal: Once Tibet achieves its aim, Zhongjie too will be in the enemy's grasp — how could he again serve us?
translations.idiomatic: Once Tibet achieves its aim, Zhongjie too will be in the enemy's grasp — how could he ever serve us again?

sentences.zh: 往吐蕃於國無有恩力，猶欲爭十姓、四鎮；

translations.literal: In the past Tibet owed the state no debt of kindness, yet still wished to contest the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Tibet owed the state no debt of gratitude, yet still sought to contest the Ten Surnames and Four Garrisons;

sentences.zh: 今若效力樹恩，則請分於闐、疏勒者，欲何理抑之？

translations.literal: If it now exerts effort and plants favor, then when it asks to divide Khotan and Kashgar — by what reasoning could we refuse?
translations.idiomatic: If it now renders service and builds up favor, then when it asks to divide Khotan and Kashgar, by what reasoning could we refuse?

sentences.zh: 且其國諸蠻及婆羅門方自嫌阻，藉令求我助討者，亦何以拒之？

translations.literal: Moreover, the various barbarian peoples and Brahmans within its realm are just now mutually suspicious and obstructive — if they should seek our aid in punitive campaigns, how could we refuse?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the various barbarian peoples and Brahmans within its realm are just now mutually suspicious and obstructive. If they should seek our aid in punitive campaigns, how could we refuse?

sentences.zh: 是以古之賢人，不願夷狄妄惠，非不欲其力，懼後求無厭，益生中國事也。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthies of old did not welcome reckless favors from the barbarians — not because they did not want their strength, but because they feared that endless demands would follow and multiply troubles for the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the worthies of old did not welcome reckless favors from the barbarians — not because they did not want their strength, but because they feared endless demands would follow and multiply troubles for the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為用吐蕃之力，不見其便。

translations.literal: This foolish subject believes that employing Tibetan force offers no visible advantage.
translations.idiomatic: This subject believes that employing Tibetan force offers no visible advantage.

sentences.zh: 又請阿史那獻者，豈非以可汗子孫能招綏十姓乎？

translations.literal: As for again proposing Ashina Xian — is it not on the grounds that a khan's descendant can win and pacify the Ten Surnames?
translations.idiomatic: As for again proposing Ashina Xian — is it not on the grounds that a khan's descendant can win over and pacify the Ten Surnames?

sentences.zh: 且斛瑟羅及懷道與獻父元慶、叔仆羅、兄俀子，俱可汗子孫也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Kuseluo and Huaidao, together with Xian's father Yuancqing, his uncle Puluo, and his elder brother Yizi, were all descendants of khans.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Kuseluo and Huaidao, together with Xian's father Yuancqing, his uncle Puluo, and his elder brother Yizi, were all descendants of khans.

sentences.zh: 往四鎮以他匐十姓之亂，請元慶為可汗，卒亦不能招來，而元慶沒賊，四鎮淪陷。

translations.literal: Formerly, because of the disturbance among the Ten Surnames under Tafu, Yuancqing was requested as khan — in the end he could not summon them either. Yuancqing perished among the enemy and the Four Garrisons fell.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, because of the disturbance among the Ten Surnames under Tafu, Yuancqing was requested as khan, but in the end he could not win them over either. Yuancqing perished among the enemy and the Four Garrisons fell.

sentences.zh: 忠節亦嘗請以斛瑟羅及懷道為可汗矣，十姓未附而碎葉幾危。

translations.literal: Zhongjie also once requested Kuseluo and Huaidao as khans — the Ten Surnames did not submit and Suyab was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie also once requested Kuseluo and Huaidao as khans, but the Ten Surnames did not submit and Suyab was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 又吐蕃亦嘗以俀子、仆羅並拔布為可汗矣，亦不能得十姓而皆自亡滅，此非它，其子孫無惠下之才，恩義素絕故也。

translations.literal: Tibet too once made Yizi, Puluo, and Babu khans — they also could not obtain the Ten Surnames and all perished on their own. This was nothing else: their descendants lacked talent for showing kindness to those below, and grace and duty had long been severed.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet too once made Yizi, Puluo, and Babu khans, but they also could not obtain the Ten Surnames and all perished on their own. This was nothing else: their descendants lacked the talent to win loyalty from those below, and grace and duty had long been severed.

sentences.zh: 豈止不能招懷，且復為四鎮患，則冊可汗子孫其效固試矣。

translations.literal: Far from being unable to win them over, they again became a calamity for the Four Garrisons — the effect of enfeoffing khan's descendants has indeed been tested.
translations.idiomatic: Far from winning them over, they again became a calamity for the Four Garrisons — the effect of enfeoffing khan's descendants has indeed been tested.

sentences.zh: 獻又遠於其父兄，人心何繇即附，若兵力足取十姓，不必要須可汗子孫也。

translations.literal: Xian is even more distant from his father and elder brothers — by what way could hearts immediately attach to him? If military strength suffices to take the Ten Surnames, a khan's descendant is not necessarily required.
translations.idiomatic: Xian is even more distant from his father and elder brothers — by what means could hearts immediately attach to him? If military strength suffices to take the Ten Surnames, a khan's descendant is not necessarily required.

sentences.zh: 又請以郭虔瓘搜兵稅馬於拔汗那。

translations.literal: Again they request that Guo Qianjin levy troops and requisition horses in Bohuana.
translations.idiomatic: Again they request that Guo Qianjin levy troops and requisition horses in Ferghana.

sentences.zh: 往虔瓘已嘗與忠節擅入其國，臣時在疏勒，不聞得一甲一馬，而拔汗那挾忿侵擾，南導吐蕃。

translations.literal: Formerly Qianjin already entered that country without authorization together with Zhongjie. I was at Kashgar at the time and heard of not a single suit of armor or horse obtained — yet Bohuana, nursing resentment, raided and disturbed, and guided Tibet from the south.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Qianjin already entered that country without authorization together with Zhongjie. I was at Kashgar at the time and heard of not a single suit of armor or horse obtained, yet Ferghana, nursing resentment, raided and disturbed the frontier and guided Tibet from the south.

sentences.zh: 將俀子，以擾四鎮。

translations.literal: taking Yizi's son to harass the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: using Yizi's son to trouble the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 且虔瓘往至拔汗那國，四面無助，若履虛邑，猶引俀子為敝。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Qianjin went to Bohuana he had no help on any side — as if treading an empty settlement — yet still brought Yizi in as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Qianjin went to Ferghana he had no help on any side, as if treading an empty settlement, yet still brought Yizi in as an ally.

sentences.zh: 況今北有娑葛，知虔瓘之西，必引以相援，拔汗那倚堅城而抗於內，突厥邀伺於外，虔瓘等豈能復如往年得安易之幸哉？

translations.literal: How much more now, with Suoge to the north — knowing Qianjin was going west, he would surely lead aid — Bohuana relying on strong walls to resist from within and the Turks lying in wait without: could Qianjin and the others again enjoy the easy good fortune of former years?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so now, with Suoge to the north — knowing Qianjin was going west, he would surely bring aid — Ferghana relying on strong walls to resist from within and the Turks lying in wait without: could Qianjin and the others again enjoy the easy good fortune of former years?

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.

sentences.zh: 楚客等因建遣攝御史中丞馮嘉賓持節安撫闕啜，以御史呂守素處置四鎮，以牛師獎為安西副都護，代元振領甘、涼兵，召吐蕃並力擊娑葛。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke and the others therefore proposed dispatching Acting Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin with credentials to pacify Quechuo, censor Lü Shousu to administer the Four Garrisons, and Niu Shijiang as Vice Protector of Anxi to replace Yuanzhen in commanding the Gan and Liang troops, and summoning Tibet to join forces in attacking Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke and the others therefore proposed dispatching Acting Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin with credentials to pacify Quechuo, censor Lü Shousu to administer the Four Garrisons, and Niu Shijiang as Vice Protector of Anxi to replace Yuanzhen in commanding the Gan and Liang troops, and summoning Tibet to join forces in attacking Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛之使娑臘知楚客謀，馳報之。

translations.literal: Suoge's envoy Suola learned of Chuke's plot and rode post-haste to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge's envoy Suola learned of Chuke's plot and rode post-haste to report it.

sentences.zh: 娑葛怒，即發兵出安西、撥換、焉耆、疏勒各五千騎。

translations.literal: Suoge was enraged and immediately sent out troops from Anxi, Bokhwan, Kucha, and Kashgar — five thousand horsemen from each.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge was enraged and immediately sent out troops from Anxi, Bokhwan, Kucha, and Kashgar — five thousand horsemen from each.

sentences.zh: 於是闕啜在計舒河與嘉賓會，娑葛兵奄至，禽闕啜，殺嘉賓，又殺呂守素於僻城、牛師獎於火燒城，遂陷安西，四鎮路絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quechuo met with Jiabin on the Jishu River; Suoge's troops suddenly arrived, captured Quechuo, killed Jiabin, also killed Lü Shousu at Picheng and Niu Shijiang at Huoshaocheng, then overran Anxi — communication with the Four Garrisons was severed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Quechuo met with Jiabin on the Jishu River. Suoge's troops suddenly arrived, captured Quechuo, killed Jiabin, also killed Lü Shousu at Picheng and Niu Shijiang at Huoshaocheng, then overran Anxi, and communication with the Four Garrisons was severed.

sentences.zh: 元振屯疏勒水上，未敢動。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen encamped at the waters of Kashgar and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen encamped at the waters of Kashgar and did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 楚客復表周以悌代元振，且以阿史那獻為十姓可汗，置軍焉耆以取娑葛。

translations.literal: Chuke again memorialized to replace Yuanzhen with Zhou Yiti, and to make Ashina Xian khan of the Ten Surnames, stationing troops at Kucha to take Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke again memorialized to replace Yuanzhen with Zhou Yiti, to make Ashina Xian khan of the Ten Surnames, and to station troops at Kucha to take Suoge.

sentences.zh: 娑葛遺元振書，且言：「無仇於唐，而楚客等受闕啜金，欲加兵擊滅我，故懼死而鬥。

translations.literal: Suoge sent a letter to Yuanzhen, saying: "I bear no grudge against Tang, but Chuke and the others received Quechuo's gold and wished to send troops to attack and destroy me — therefore, fearing death, I fight.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge sent a letter to Yuanzhen, saying, "I bear no grudge against Tang, but Chuke and the others received Quechuo's gold and wished to send troops to attack and destroy me — therefore, fearing death, I fight.

sentences.zh: 且請斬楚客。」

translations.literal: And I request that Chuke be executed."
translations.idiomatic: I also request that Chuke be executed."

sentences.zh: 元振奏其狀。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen memorialized the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen memorialized the facts.

sentences.zh: 楚客大怒，誣元振有異圖，召將罪之。

translations.literal: Chuke was furious, slandered Yuanzhen as harboring treacherous designs, and summoned him to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was furious, slandered Yuanzhen as harboring treacherous designs, and summoned him to be punished.

sentences.zh: 元振使子鴻間道奏乞留定西土，不敢歸京師。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen sent his son Hong by a secret route to memorialize, begging to remain and secure the western lands, not daring to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen sent his son Hong by a secret route to memorialize, begging to remain and secure the western lands, not daring to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以悌乃得罪，流白州，而赦娑葛。

translations.literal: Yiti was then found guilty and exiled to Baizhou, and Suoge was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yiti was then found guilty and exiled to Baizhou, and Suoge was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，召為太仆卿。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Yuanzhen was summoned as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Yuanzhen was summoned to serve as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 將行，安西酋長有剺面哭送者，旌節下玉門關，去涼州猶八百里，城中爭具壺漿歡迎，都督嗟嘆以聞。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Anxi chieftains came with lacerated faces weeping to see him off. When his banner and credentials passed below Yumen Pass, still eight hundred li from Liangzhou, the city competed to prepare pots of drink to welcome him in celebration. The Protector-General sighed in admiration and reported this.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Anxi chieftains came with lacerated faces weeping to see him off. When his banner and credentials passed below Yumen Pass, still eight hundred li from Liangzhou, the city competed to prepare pots of drink to welcome him in celebration. The Protector-General sighed in admiration and reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，進同中書門下三品，遷吏部尚書，封館陶縣男。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was promoted to Co-acting with the Secretariat and Chancellery as Third Rank, transferred to Minister of the Civil Service, and enfeoffed as Baron of Guantao County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he was promoted to co-acting with the Secretariat and Chancellery as third rank, transferred to Minister of the Civil Service, and enfeoffed as Baron of Guantao County.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，為朔方軍大總管，築豐安、定遠城，兵得保頓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian he became Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army, built Feng'an and Dingyuan cities, and the troops were able to rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian he became Grand Commander of the Shuofang Army, built Feng'an and Dingyuan cities, and the troops were able to encamp in safety.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兵部尚書復同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The following year, as Minister of War he again served Co-acting with the Secretariat and Chancellery as Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as Minister of War he again served as co-acting with the Secretariat and Chancellery as third rank.

sentences.zh: 玄宗誅太平公主也，睿宗禦承天門，諸宰相走伏外省，獨元振總兵扈帝，事定，宿中書者十四夕乃休。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong executed Princess Taiping, Ruizong took the throne at Chengtian Gate; the chief ministers fled and prostrated themselves outside the Secretariat — only Yuanzhen commanded troops to escort the Emperor. When affairs were settled, he lodged at the Secretariat for fourteen nights before resting.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong executed Princess Taiping, Ruizong took the throne at Chengtian Gate. The chief ministers fled and prostrated themselves outside the Secretariat; only Yuanzhen commanded troops to escort the Emperor. When affairs were settled, he lodged at the Secretariat for fourteen nights before resting.

sentences.zh: 進封代國公，實封四百戶，賜一子官，物千段。

translations.literal: He was promoted in enfeoffment to Duke of Dai State, with four hundred taxable households, one son granted an office, and one thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in enfeoffment to Duke of Dai, with four hundred taxable households, one son granted an office, and one thousand rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 俄又兼御史大夫，復為朔方大總管，以備突厥。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and again became Grand Commander of Shuofang to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and again became Grand Commander of Shuofang to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 未行，會玄宗講武驪山，既三令，帝親鼓之，元振遽奏禮止，帝怒軍容不整，引坐纛下，將斬之。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, Xuanzong held a martial review at Mount Li. After the third command the Emperor personally beat the drum; Yuanzhen abruptly memorialized that the rites should stop. The Emperor, angered that the troops' bearing was not orderly, had him brought to sit beneath the command banner and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Xuanzong held a martial review at Mount Li. After the third command the Emperor personally beat the drum; Yuanzhen abruptly memorialized that the rites should stop. The Emperor, angered that the troops' bearing was not orderly, had him brought to sit beneath the command banner and was about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求、張說扣馬諫曰：「元振有大功，雖得罪，當宥。」

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying: "Yuanzhen has great merit — though he has offended, he should be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying, "Yuanzhen has great merit — though he has offended, he should be spared."

sentences.zh: 乃赦死，流新州。

translations.literal: He was spared death and exiled to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared death and exiled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元元年，帝思舊功，起為饒州司馬，怏怏不得誌，道病卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyuan the Emperor recalled his old service and recalled him as Vice-Governor of Raozhou. Discontent and unable to fulfill his ambition, he fell ill on the road and died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyuan the Emperor recalled his old service and appointed him Vice-Governor of Raozhou. Discontent and unable to fulfill his ambition, he fell ill on the road and died at age fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 十年，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Ten years later he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元振雖少雄邁，及貴，居處乃儉約，手不置書，人莫見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Though bold and sweeping in youth, once elevated Yuanzhen's dwelling was frugal and sparing; his hand never held a book, and no one ever saw him show pleasure or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Though bold and sweeping in youth, once elevated Yuanzhen lived frugally; his hand never held a book, and no one ever saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 建宅宣陽裏，未嘗一至諸院廄。

translations.literal: He built a mansion in Xuanyang Ward but never once went to any of its side courts or stables.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mansion in Xuanyang Ward but never once went to any of its side courts or stables.

sentences.zh: 自朝還，對親欣欣，退就室，儼如也。

translations.literal: Returning from court he would face his kin with cheer; withdrawing to his chamber he was solemn as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from court he would face his kin with cheer; withdrawing to his chamber he was solemn as ever.

sentences.zh: 距國初仕至宰相而親具者，唯元振雲。

translations.literal: From the founding of the dynasty until one rose to chief minister while his parents were still alive — only Yuanzhen, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the dynasty until one rose to chief minister while one's parents were still alive — only Yuanzhen, it is said.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：魏、韋皆感概而奮，似矣。

translations.literal: The appraising comment says: Wei and Wei both were stirred by emotion to strive — they seem so.
translations.idiomatic: The appraising comment says: Wei and Wei both were stirred by emotion to strive — so it seems.

sentences.zh: 及在惸上側臣間，臨機會，不一引手揕奸邪之謀，誠可鄙哉。

translations.literal: Yet when among the isolated sovereign and the courtiers at his side, at critical moments they never once raised a hand to thwart the schemes of the wicked — truly contemptible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when among the isolated sovereign and the courtiers at his side, at critical moments they never once raised a hand to thwart the schemes of the wicked — truly contemptible.

sentences.zh: 至牴後艷主以烝譖撼宗社，亦不肯從也。

translations.literal: Even when resisting the queen dowager's licentious slander that shook the altars of state, they would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Even when resisting the dowager empress's licentious slander that shook the altars of state, they would not consent.

sentences.zh: 古所謂具臣者，諒乎！

translations.literal: The so-called "complete minister" of antiquity — can one believe it!
translations.idiomatic: The so-called "complete minister" of antiquity — can one believe it!

sentences.zh: 元振功顯節完，一跌未復，世恨其蚤歿雲。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's merit was manifest and his integrity whole; he fell once and did not rise again — the world regrets that he died so early, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen's merit was manifest and his integrity whole; he fell once and did not rise again — the world regrets that he died so young, it is said.
